description:

2027 Clinical Pharmacology Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
AbbVie’s Clinical Pharmacology (ClinPharm) organization provides critical scientific support for all phases of pharmaceutical research and development in all divisions of the business. ClinPharm leads the design, execution, and interpretation of all clinical pharmacology Phase 1 studies, and exposure-clinical response modeling and simulation to optimize dose selection and trial design. The team also integrates data from multiple sources including preclinical and clinical pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, dosing compliance/adherence, effective and toxic exposures, financial metrics, and overall cost/benefit. Another key responsibility of the team is to present the data to regulatory authorities world-wide and authors more than half of the clinical summary documents for global regulatory submissions.
Internship projects could vary and are dependent on therapeutic area needs. Current therapeutic areas supported include Immunology, Oncology, Neurology, and Specialty assets.
Key project responsibilities include:
Analysis of literature and in-house proprietary data
Dose- and Exposure- Safety & Efficacy Endpoint Analysis
Database analyses
Development of mathematical models (e.g. PK/PD, Population PK, etc.)
Conducting simulations using mathematical models
Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD)
Clinical study design
Presentation to the broader team at the conclusion of the assignment
Publication of authorized analyses
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PharmD or PhD in Pharmacokinetics, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, or other related field
Must be returning to university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Experience analyzing scientific literature and data, including database and dose- or exposure-response (safety and efficacy) analyses
Familiarity with developing and running mathematical models and simulations (e.g., PK/PD, Population PK), ideally in a Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) context
Understanding of clinical study design

Purpose
Own the end-to-end governance, health, and continuous improvement of assigned clinical business processes, ensuring processes are inspection-ready, scalable, and aligned to enterprise priorities and regulatory expectations. Partner across Clinical Development Operations and enabling functions to translate strategy into clear process outcomes, drive adoption through change management and learning alignment, and monitor process performance signals to proactively address risk and improve execution. Role may be filled as a Sr. BPO depending on experience and process areas.
Responsibilities
Serve as the accountable owner for assigned clinical business processes across their lifecycle (Engage → Evaluate → Execute → Measure → Sustain), defining process scope, intended outcomes, and decision rights.
Establish and maintain an end-to-end process governance model (standards, forums, escalations, and stakeholder alignment) to ensure consistent global execution and a unified, single voice to the business.
Own process health and sustainability by defining and monitoring key process signals/metrics, identifying emerging issues and risks, and driving timely mitigation and continuous improvement.
Translate business and regulatory needs into clear process requirements and partner with Process Excellence roles (e.g., process design/engineering) to ensure documentation is complete, consistent, and inspection-ready.
Act as the authoritative point of contact for process questions within the domain; curate and maintain process knowledge content and ensure availability of fit-for-purpose guidance for end users.
Lead cross-functional stakeholder engagement to align priorities, trade-offs, and adoption plans, ensuring the right SMEs are engaged at the right time and decisions are transparent and durable.
Partner with stakeholders to ensure change narratives, communications, and role-based training enable effective adoption and sustained performance.
Coordinate and coach a domain SME network to support process adherence, identify improvement opportunities, and reinforce standard ways of working.
Partner with system and business owners to ensure process-to-system alignment, impact assessment for changes, and effective implementation support (e.g., acceptance criteria, UAT input, and readiness planning).
Embed innovation and digital/AI enablement into process oversight and improvements where appropriate, ensuring changes are controlled, compliant, and measurable.

Minimum of 8 years clinical process management experience required with demonstrated experience owning and governing end-to-end business processes in a regulated environment (clinical development, GxP, quality systems, or similar).
Strong understanding of clinical development operations and the regulatory/inspection context; ability to apply this knowledge to process decisions and risk management.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional alignment and stakeholder management, including conflict resolution and escalation when needed.

Define and evaluate security architecture for the end-user device estate — workstation and laptop hardening, EDR/endpoint protection (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender), data protection, and configuration baselines.

Due Diligence. Act as the primary point of contact for due diligence efforts, and the representative of Commercial BTS within the broader BTS community of M&A practitioners.

As Director, Global Alliances, Neuroscience , you will shape and manage strategic external collaborations from discovery through commercialization, with primary responsibility for AbbVie’s Neuroscience partnerships. AbbVie is the industry leader in neuroscience by sales, with a broad and growing portfolio spanning neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, and other strategic priorities.
You will lead complex, high-value alliances that advance AbbVie’s neuroscience pipeline and marketed portfolio. Represent AbbVie at corporate partnering events to strengthen relationships with current and prospective partners.

title: Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
This position is part of AbbVie's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team within Business Technology Solutions. The Identity & Access Management (IAM) team is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of the organization's IAM strategy, ensuring secure, efficient, and compliant access to systems and data. The NHI and Cloud IAM function addresses one of the fastest-growing attack surfaces in enterprise security—machine identities now outnumber human ones, and the rapid expansion of AI agents is accelerating that trend. This role does not own the AI agent or cloud platforms themselves—those are owned by partner teams across BTS—but it is the IAM team's authoritative voice on how those platforms must integrate with identity governance, and it is accountable for ensuring that no non-human identity operates outside of AbbVie's visibility or control.
Take the next step in your career with an organization that strategically invests in the long-term health of the company, its technology and its people. The AbbVie Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation necessary for our treatments to positively impact patients' lives. In the role of Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead, you'll tackle one of the most complex and rapidly evolving challenges in enterprise security: establishing a unified strategy for non-human identities, AI agent governance, and cloud IAM—bridging today's fragmented landscape into a coherent, observable, and future-ready program. This is a senior, highly technical role that requires both architectural depth and the organizational influence to drive accountability across the teams that own AI, agentic, and cloud platforms—ensuring that every non-human identity is visible, governed, and secured from AbbVie's IAM systems.
In this role, you'll be responsible for:
Define and drive the enterprise Non-Human Identity (NHI) strategy—rapidly assessing all in-flight initiatives across the organization, rationalizing overlapping efforts, and establishing a centralized, authoritative governance program covering all machine identities across on-premises, cloud, and agentic environments
Build and maintain a comprehensive NHI registry encompassing service accounts, APIs, bots, application identities, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI agents—ensuring every non-human identity is discovered, inventoried, classified, and continuously governed within IAM systems
Own AbbVie's identity governance posture for AI agents: while the creation and operation of AI agent platforms is owned by other teams, this role is accountable for ensuring those platforms integrate with IAM—so that every AI agent is inventoried in the NHI registry, mapped to its owning human or system identity, governed through appropriate access controls, and visible for security monitoring
Proactively discover and identify new AI agents and agentic workloads as they are introduced across the enterprise; partner with AI platform, cloud, and business teams to ensure timely onboarding into the NHI governance framework, and drive remediations or mappings where gaps exist
Serve as the IAM point of accountability for all agent-related identity questions: defining standards for how agents authenticate, what credentials they use, how those credentials are secured, and how agent activity is observable from an identity and access perspective
Establish centralized NHI observability by driving integration between IAM platforms and external systems—including AWS, Azure, GCP, and agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock, or similar)—so that IAM maintains a living, authoritative view of all non-human identities regardless of where they originate
Design and implement modern NHI credential security controls including just-in-time (JIT) access, dynamic secrets, short-lived certificates, automated credential rotation, and runtime authentication—reducing standing privilege for machine identities to near zero where possible
Assess the current tooling landscape for NHI and cloud IAM; determine whether existing platforms can be extended or reconfigured, or whether new capabilities are needed; and build a pragmatic, phased modernization roadmap
Own and evolve the Cloud IAM and IGA strategy, closing the integration gap between cloud-native identity platforms (AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM) and AbbVie's central IAM/IGA tools—ensuring cloud identities, entitlements, and access certifications are governed consistently and automatically
Design cloud identity governance frameworks including role-based access models, entitlement management, access certifications, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud environments
Drive cross-functional alignment across IAM, AI Platform, Cloud, Security Architecture, Compliance, Audit, and business teams—translating complex, fast-moving requirements into executable roadmap priorities and holding partner teams accountable for IAM integration commitments
Establish KPIs and maturity metrics for the NHI and Cloud IAM program, providing executive-level visibility into inventory completeness, risk posture, program progress, and open gaps
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements (SOX, GDPR, PCI-DSS) for machine identities and cloud access controls; respond to and remediate audit findings
Manage budget, resources, and vendor relationships for all NHI and Cloud IAM technologies and solutions
Lead and mentor a team of technical specialists, cultivating a culture of proactive governance, automation, and continuous improvement
Bachelor's degree with 8 years experience OR 7 years of experience OR PhD with 3 years experience
Hands-on experience with non-human identity management, cloud IAM, or machine identity governance in large enterprise environments
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing NHI programs—including service accounts, API credentials, application identities, and/or automated/agentic workloads
Strong hands-on expertise with cloud IAM frameworks: AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, and/or GCP IAM, including integration with central IGA platforms
Experience designing and implementing cloud IGA processes: entitlement management, access certifications, role-based access models, and least-privilege enforcement in cloud environments
Proven experience with secrets management platforms and modern credential security patterns (JIT access, short-lived certificates, dynamic secrets, automated rotation)
Architecture-level understanding of identity federation, service-to-service authentication, and cloud-native identity patterns (OAuth, OIDC, SAML, workload identity)
Strong track record of driving complex, cross-functional programs in matrixed organizations—including influencing and holding accountable teams that are not direct reports
Demonstrated ability to proactively identify governance gaps, drive partner teams to remediate, and establish scalable, automated processes to prevent recurrence
Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build alignment across organizational boundaries
Beneficial:
Familiarity with AI agent platforms and their identity/credential patterns (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock agents, or similar agentic frameworks)
Experience building NHI discovery and inventory capabilities, including integration with platforms not originally designed for identity governance
Familiarity with containerization and Kubernetes service account management
Hands-on experience with IGA platforms and their cloud connectors (Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent)
Scripting and automation experience (PowerShell, Python, Terraform, or other IaC tools)
Knowledge of certificate management, PKI infrastructure, and API security platforms
Understanding of CIS, NIST, and other cloud security compliance frameworks
Industry certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS/Azure/GCP security certifications, or equivalent
Experience in the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry
Tools and skills you will use in this role:
Cloud IAM platforms: AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM — and their integration with enterprise IGA
Secrets management platforms: HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, or equivalent
IGA platforms with cloud connectors: Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent
NHI discovery, inventory, and governance tooling
Just-in-time access, dynamic secrets, and runtime authentication frameworks
Integration APIs and connectors for agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock) — for identity inventory and observability, not platform ownership
Service-to-service authentication protocols: OAuth, OIDC, SAML, workload identity federation
Containerization and Kubernetes service account management
CI/CD pipeline integrations for identity and secrets (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Terraform)
Scripting and automation: PowerShell, Python, Infrastructure as Code
Certificate management and PKI
Audit and compliance reporting for cloud and NHI controls
Strong architectural thinking, cross-functional influence, and executive communication skills

The Regional Medical Outcomes Science Liaison (Regional MOSL) is the regional scientific expert responsible for leading advanced, non-promotional, outcomes-focused scientific engagement with regional healthcare decision makers. The role integrates clinical evidence, real-world data, and health economics and outcomes research to inform product access and population-level decision making, evidence needs, and AbbVie medical planning. The Regional MOSL proactively identifies key regional healthcare decision makers (HCDMs), serves as the primary medical liaison between AbbVie and HCDMs, builds strong relationships to understand customer needs, and facilitates generation of real-world evidence (RWE) consistent with approved therapeutic area medical planning.
The Regional MOSL advances field scientific strategies.
Serve as the Medical lead within the integrated account team for assigned accounts, playing an integral role in appropriate planning, strategy development and execution.
Participate across assigned therapeutic area and healthcare landscape strategic committees.
Customized communication of scientific, health outcomes, and health policy information to HCDMs and influencers.  Document and communicate meaningful observations that lead to Scientific Intelligence on a regular basis; Identify emerging scientific, health economic, and health policy trends and integrate gaps and learnings into functional strategy and objectives.
Primary interface and initial point of contact for small-scale, RWE opportunities with regional level HCDMs.
Anticipate, identify and address population-level scientific, outcomes research, and health policy needs of customers serving as the trusted advisor to the customer.  Leverage internal and external resources to meet customer needs.
Facilitate scientific exchange, as necessary, between AbbVie Medical Leadership, including Medical Affairs, TA Medical Directors, and HEOR with accounts to support internal and external customer objectives.
Maintain and continually enhance clinical, scientific, and healthcare landscape expertise.  Participate in various therapeutic advisory activities involving both marketed and investigational products, spanning the full product life-cycle.
Engage regional healthcare decision makers in compliant, peer level scientific exchange integrating clinical evidence, health economics and outcomes research, and real-world evidence.

Advanced innovative problem solving, critical thinking, and communication skills.

Advanced ability to network and collaborate effectively across multiple levels within an organization.

Interprets regulatory, policy, and access landscape considerations to support compliant engagement and inform regional planning.
Defines and communicates holistic value propositions by integrating clinical, economic, and humanistic evidence relevant to regional healthcare decision making.
Uses appropriate evidence sources, including real-world evidence and health economics data, to support outcomes-focused dialogue.
Translates regional Scientific Intelligence into actionable input that informs medical planning, evidence needs, and access strategies.
Applies strategic thinking to align scientific engagement with regional objectives, account priorities, and healthcare system needs.
Engages in effective, two-way scientific communication to build trusted relationships with healthcare decision makers.
Collaborates across cross-functional partners and the In-Field Team (IFT) to support aligned execution and Scientific Intelligence.

This individual is recognized as very knowledgeable in their discipline and in regulatory affairs submission support for emerging markets.
Serves as primary point of contact with Affiliate Regulatory team for country/region specific document and sample requests to support local regulatory submission activities for new product registrations or to maintain existing product registrations.

Collaborates with internal teams across AbbVie sites and with Third-Party Manufacturers (TPMs) to obtain documents such as GMP Certificates and Manufacturing Licenses.
Communicates and coordinates with external vendors to ensure legalization of documents in accordance with specific country requirements.

Maintains up-to-date status tracking in departmental systems and tools; provides regular status updates and may generate reports/dashboards to support delivery timelines and service level metrics; offers input to global teams on submission timelines and deliverables.
Manages and coordinates multiple concurrent requests and deliverables to ensure timely execution of tasks with varying business impact; proactively anticipates obstacles and contributes solutions within the team.

Independently manages and prioritizes daily assignments, keeps stakeholders informed on the status of requests, and escalates issues as necessary to ensure tasks are completed on time and in accordance with submission deadlines

Required Experience: Two years’ pharmaceutical or industry related experience

description:

At AbbVie, the Precision Medicine Department is dedicated to advancing drug development and elevating patient care by deepening our understanding of disease biology and pioneering personalized treatment solutions. Within our Immunology Translational Research team, we leverage cutting-edge technologies to unravel disease mechanisms, discover novel biomarkers, and validate targets across our robust immunology pipeline.
We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Scientist I with profound expertise in immunology or immuno-oncology and a passion for translational research. In this pivotal role, the candidate will spearhead the development of clinical biomarker analytic strategies for inflammatory and autoimmune diseases—spanning Dermatology, Gastroenterology, Rheumatology, and Fibrosis—from late-stage discovery through clinical trials. Joining a dynamic and expanding research group, the candidate will collaborate seamlessly with cross-functional internal and external teams to drive our translational biomarker initiatives forward.

Develop preclinical, patient-derived disease models and design controlled studies to elucidate drug mechanisms, advance PD biomarker development, and test combination hypotheses.
Independently lead the design, execution, and analysis of complex datasets from flow cytometry, cytokine profiling, and advanced genomic profiling (including single-cell RNA-Seq and spatial transcriptomics/proteomics).

Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.

Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements

Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.

Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred

Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.

The Quantitative, Translational and ADME Sciences (QTAS) organization at AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated Senior Scientist II to join the Non-Regulated Bioanalysis team in North Chicago. This lab-based role provides hands-on scientific and operational bioanalytical support for discovery and preclinical programs across a diverse and evolving portfolio.
The successful candidate will independently lead bioanalytical method development, optimization, troubleshooting, and implementation using mass spectrometry-based approaches. This individual will apply sound scientific judgment to address complex analytical challenges, manage an assigned portfolio of studies, and help advance fit-for-purpose bioanalytical strategies and team capabilities. The role requires effective work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, balancing responsiveness to evolving program needs with scientific rigor, data quality, and sound judgment.
Core Responsibilities
Independently develop, optimize, qualify, and apply fit-for-purpose LC/MS–based quantitative bioanalytical methods to support non-regulated discovery and preclinical studies.
Lead technical problem-solving for complex bioanalytical challenges, including sample preparation, extraction, chromatographic separation, detection, quantitation, and data interpretation across a range of modalities and biological matrices.
Manage bioanalytical support for an assigned portfolio of studies, effectively prioritizing work to provide responsive, high-quality data delivery while maintaining scientific rigor and alignment with project timelines.
Independently design and execute experiments to evaluate assay performance, troubleshoot instrument, assay, and data-quality issues; implement appropriate corrective actions and communicate risks, findings, and recommendations in a timely manner.
Stay current with advances in bioanalytical science, evaluate, implement, and help establish analytical technologies, methodologies, and workflows that improve capability, efficiency, robustness, or scientific understanding.
Partner with QTAS representatives, project teams, and other cross-functional stakeholders to define bioanalytical needs, align on study objectives, interpret results, and provide clear scientific recommendations.
Maintain accurate experimental records and study documentation; provide technical mentorship and contribute to a collaborative, high-performing laboratory environment.
PhD in analytical chemistry, bioanalytical chemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related field with 3+ years of relevant experience; or MS with 10+ years; or BS with 12+ years of relevant academic and/or industry experience.
Strong hands-on experience in LC-MS/MS–based quantitative bioanalysis, including method development, optimization, troubleshooting, and data interpretation.
Demonstrated ability to independently plan, execute, interpret, and communicate bioanalytical experiments supporting discovery or preclinical programs.
Experience addressing complex bioanalytical challenges involving sample preparation, extraction, chromatography, mass spectrometric detection, and quantitative analysis.
Proficiency operating modern LC-MS/MS platforms and associated acquisition, processing, and data-review software.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple studies or competing priorities while maintaining scientific rigor, data quality, and timeline accountability.
Ability to prioritize competing requests, respond constructively to changing program needs, and deliver reliable results with appropriate urgency in a dynamic research environment.
Strong scientific judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify risks, develop practical solutions, and influence technical decisions.
Effective written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate scientific findings and recommendations to technical and cross-functional audiences.
Proven ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic, interdisciplinary research environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting bioanalysis across more than one therapeutic modality or working with technically challenging analytes and biological matrices is required.
Experience in regulated bioanalysis, translational bioanalysis, or a contract research organization environment is preferred.
Experience implementing automated sample-preparation platforms, advanced sample-preparation workflows, or laboratory-process improvements is a plus.
Working knowledge of pharmacokinetics, including study-design considerations and interpretation of PK-related bioanalytical data.
Demonstrated record of evaluating, introducing, or scaling new analytical technologies or workflows.
Experience mentoring junior colleagues, leading technical workstreams, or serving as a scientific point of contact for project teams.

Builds productive relationships within the team and across functions to enable high-quality scientific execution and timely decision-making.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
Airbnb’s Legal Department is a global team that will require working with diverse international colleagues around the world. The successful candidate will be someone who is adaptable, collaborative and embodies Airbnb’s Core Values. Candidates will be required to approach complex legal issues with a balance for local and global perspectives, while being adaptable to cultural differences and nuances. A genuine and demonstrated interest in Airbnb and a commitment to ethics, integrity and fostering a workplace that emphasizes diversity and belonging is a must.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb’s Legal team embodies the company’s innovative, forward-thinking spirit. At the frontier of the new sharing economy, Airbnb is breaking new ground in matters of policy, law, and government relations. Where some see obstacles, we see the opportunity to find creative, practical solutions, right at the cutting edge. Our adventurous, fast-moving legal team is committed to building a team of talented, collaborative and self-motivated legal professionals across the globe who believe in Airbnb’s mission and leading as a 21st century company.
The Difference You Will Make:
Airbnb is looking for an experienced litigator to join our Risk and Regulatory group. Reporting to Airbnb's Associate General Counsel, Litigation & Policy, the Lead Counsel, Litigation will own high-stakes disputes, investigations, and strategic counseling from first assessment through resolution, directing outside counsel and shaping our approach at every stage.
This role is for you if you work well with business partners, bring a steady and positive presence, and thrive in a collaborative environment. Where some see obstacles, you see room for creative, practical solutions that move Airbnb's global mission forward. You are energized by complex disputes, comfortable engaging regulatory and administrative bodies, and ready to be a trusted voice on the matters that matter most. As Lead Counsel, Litigation you will:

Handle highly sensitive matters with a strategic mindset and strong judgment.
Manage outside counsel across the full life of a case: budget, strategy, work product, and results.
Drive matters through every stage, from early strategic case assessment, discovery, witness preparation, depositions, dispositive motions, trial, mediation, and settlement recommendations.
Proactively identify and resolve potential disputes, giving business clients practical risk mitigation advice that supports their objectives.
Partner with public policy, compliance, and legal colleagues inside and outside Airbnb to solve problems that cross functions and borders.
Analyze legal risk across the business, including in the development of new products and services.
Build processes and procedures that scale with a rapidly growing global business.

J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials.

Sound judgment and discretion in handling highly sensitive matters and difficult subject matter.

description:

We're helping business and field teams use AI to take on high volume-low value tasks, and helping product teams understand whether an AI feature works before it reaches our users. Day to day, we move manual review processes to AI and put people where their judgment matters most. We design new workflows so AI does the work from the start. We also build the labeled datasets that show whether the AI is right, and we keep everything running as models and policies change. Our methods and projects change as the models do, and we expect the scope of this role to grow with them.
The Difference You Will Make
You'd work with whichever team has a problem AI could take on, whether that's a business team with a process that's slow, expensive or inconsistent, or a product team getting an AI feature ready to launch. The job looks much the same either way. You start with how the work really gets done, build an AI version of it, and test it until you trust the results. Then you graduate it and use what worked on the next problem. The mix of projects will keep changing as AI takes on more of the work, so we care more about how you work than about a fixed list of projects. This is a hands-on role. You design and build the workflow, prove it works with data, and ship it with engineering and product.
A Typical Day
Drive the AI workflows and features we support from design to launch, defining the quality bar and measurement plan with engineering, product and business partners.
Prioritize projects by business impact, making trade-offs in partnership with your manager and the business and product leads you support.
Sit with the team that owns a problem, map how the work gets done today, and work out how AI can do it and where people step in for the hard cases.
Design and build AI workflows: write the prompts when needed, set up the pipeline and tooling, and monitor quality and drift once it's live.
Design the evaluation framework: build test sets, define accuracy and agreement metrics, and calibrate LLM judges against human reviewers.
Work with engineers on architecture and tooling decisions, and pressure-test estimates and scope.
Turn unclear guidelines into criteria a reviewer can apply consistently, working with product, Legal and Policy.
Work with subject matter experts to write labeling guidelines and produce human-verified labels on real data.
Run labeling at scale with vendor labeling teams, and check their work against agreement metrics and your own spot checks.
Work with product teams early to agree on what "good enough to launch" means for an AI feature, and bring the evidence and a recommendation for the go/no-go decision.
Build reusable evaluation and workflow components, document what you learn, and get other teams using them so the next team gets to production faster.
Keep our methods current as models, tools and policies change, and recommend what to retire when it stops working.

8+ years in product or program management, analytics, consulting or applied AI, with a proven record of taking technical programs from idea to production and owning results such as backlog, cycle time or launch speed among others.
You're strong in SQL and in the statistics of quality: accuracy, precision and recall, sampling and reviewer agreement. You pull and analyze the data yourself instead of waiting for a report.
You’ve shipped something built on AI that other people rely on, such as a workflow, an agent or an automation, and you can show the before-and-after numbers. You can tell us where it failed and what you changed.
You're technically fluent enough to pressure-test an engineering estimate, understand how prompts, pipelines and evaluations fit together, and know when a workaround is the right call.
You're curious about how work actually gets done, including the awkward exceptions, and you've taken a messy process and made it measurable. You state the desired result first and measure success in business outcomes, not features shipped.
You have good judgment on quality. You can take messy qualitative feedback, such as reviewer comments or disagreements, and boil it down to what matters and what is worth changing.
You write clearly and can work with sales, operations, PMs and engineers in the same week, getting results through people you don't manage.
You're fine being the first person on a problem, and you try things yourself instead of waiting for someone to build them.

Hands-on Python and API experience, such as scripting data pulls, calling model APIs or building small automations.
Experience with LLM evaluation: building test sets, calibrating LLM judges or fine-tuning models.
Experience with experimentation and measurement, such as A/B tests, metric design and dashboards.

description:

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's Online Data organization runs the stores behind every booking, every message, and every payment. Storage Foundation owns the engines underneath those stores. We build and operate Airbnb's source of truth databases for the company's online OLTP traffic, and we own the control plane that provisions, upgrades, and heals them. This is engine work, not fleet administration. When our engines are slow, unavailable, or wrong, so is the product.
As Senior Engineering Manager you will lead engineers across multiple teams and you will manage managers. You will own the engine strategy, the reliability commitment that every service above you depends on, and the growth of the people who do the work. Your leverage comes from the managers and technical leads on your teams, the bar you hold in design and incident reviews, and the trust you build with the teams who stake their product on us.
The Difference You Will Make:
Set the technical direction for Airbnb's online storage engines
You will set a multi-year technical vision for the engines and the control plane beneath every transactional and key value store at Airbnb, and you will make the calls that follow from it. That includes where we invest in our own engine expertise, where we buy instead of build, how we evaluate alternative engines against real production traffic, and which capabilities have to exist before a workload can safely land on us. You will also make the cost of these systems measurable and attributable, so that investment decisions rest on evidence. You will make these calls alongside senior technical leaders across Online Data and the broader Infrastructure organization.
Make reliability the ground truth of the platform
The services built on your engines commit to availability targets that only hold if the engine underneath them is better than they are. You will own that engine level commitment and the error budgets that feed every product surface above it. You will drive fault isolation so that one tenant cannot degrade everyone else, prove regional failover with scheduled production drills, and treat capacity headroom as a reliability decision. You will own incidents in your area personally, and you will turn each one into a structural fix.
Make routine work disappear
Every ticket is a product team waiting on us and an engineer pulled off platform work. You will push your teams to build API first, so that provisioning, schema changes, grants, and quotas can be driven by an engineer, a tool, or an agent without a human in the loop. You will use AI where it takes real work off your teams.
Build and grow the team
You will coach engineering managers and senior technical leads, and grow the depth of database expertise inside Airbnb. That means taking a forward view of talent needs, building a succession pipeline, hiring senior engineers who can own a complex open source codebase, and creating the conditions where people do the most technically ambitious work of their careers. You will also represent this group to executive leadership and to our customers, and you will make the case for investment in terms the business can act on.

12+ years of engineering experience with a BS or Masters, or 9+ years with a PhD, including several years managing engineers and experience managing managers or senior technical leads
Experience leading teams that build and operate Tier 0 distributed systems, with accountability for availability targets, on call health, and incident response at a company where downtime is visible to customers
Enough technical depth in databases, storage, or comparable stateful infrastructure to set direction, judge tradeoffs, and earn the trust of engineers who work on engine internals, without needing to be the architect of record
Experience making build versus buy and vendor decisions with evidence, including managing a critical vendor or open source dependency while building more capability in house
Demonstrated ability to attract, hire, and grow senior technical talent, including other managers
Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting strategy, risk, and investment return to executives and explaining complex systems to non technical partners
Strong cross functional collaboration with customer teams, peer platform teams, and partners who do not report to you, including resolving conflict before it escalates

Experience with upstream open source contribution as a team practice, not just an individual one

title: Director, Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE)
description:
**The Opportunity**
This is a greenfield role. You'll build a product management practice, shape an entirely new category at AWS, and establish the engagement model that delivers delightful outcomes enabling customers to transform themselves.
**The Role**
As the Director of Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering will lead product management for FDE, building and leading the PM team that owns the end-to-end product lifecycle from customer engagement through production delivery through optimization and self-sufficiency. Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.
This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.
Key job responsibilities
### Product Leadership
You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.
### Product & Platform Influence
You see what breaks  across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.
You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.
### Industry Practice & Productization
You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity
### Go-to-Market Partnership
You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures
About the team
95% of enterprise technology pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact. The technology works — the gap is in the last mile: getting production systems running inside complex enterprises where legacy infrastructure, regulated data, and organizational complexity collide. AWS is making a billion-dollar investment in Forward Deployed Engineering ("FDE") to close that gap, and we're hiring product leaders who will define what we build and why.

- 15+ years in product management, with significant experience in enterprise environments

title: Principal Product Manager - Tech, Sales and Financial Integrity
description:
Amazon has hundreds of millions of customers, sellers, and developers all over the world that rely on Amazon products and services. Selling Partner Services (SPS) is the organization that constantly makes high judgment decisions across a wide breadth of constituents. Preserving Trust in Amazon with every customer, every transaction, every second is our mission. We do this by identifying and removing bad actors from the platform, while supporting a best-in-class customer experience. We ensure that Amazon is a safe and trustworthy place to shop and an amazing place to build a successful business selling products.
One of the key functions within SPS is to keep the financial relationship between Amazon and its sellers secure, transparent, and trustworthy. To that end, we own controls, verification, and validation for the payment instruments sellers use to pay Amazon and get paid, preventing fraud, money laundering, and financial abuse before it reaches customers or Amazon.
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager – Technical to set the long-term vision and technical product strategy for these SPS seller experiences. The role covers Bank Account Verification (BAV), Credit Card Verification (CCV), and other related seller experiences at Amazon's scale. You'll handle highly ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations, balancing fraud prevention, regulatory compliance (KYC/AML), and seller friction for millions of selling partners worldwide. You'll partner with engineering and science teams to build machine learning–driven risk decisioning and automated verification systems that detect and stop bad actors in real time, while giving legitimate sellers a fast, low-friction onboarding and payments experience. Your decisions will directly affect seller trust, onboarding success, payment reliability, fraud losses, and the integrity of Amazon's stores.
Key job responsibilities
* Own the multi-year vision, strategy, and product tenets for payment instrument verification (BAV/CCV) and related seller financial experiences, working backwards from sellers
* Set the technical direction with engineering and science leaders. This covers scalable verification architectures, machine learning–driven risk decisioning that replaces manual reviews, and systems that adapt in real time to new fraud and abuse patterns
* Build the roadmap and investment case, and make the hard trade-offs between fraud prevention, seller friction, regulatory compliance, cost, and speed to launch
* Lead initiatives that span multiple organizations, with partners in payments, fraud and abuse prevention, risk, finance, legal, and compliance. Get many teams aligned on shared goals and mechanisms

* Write narratives (six-pagers, PR/FAQs, planning documents) that garner support from senior product and tech leaders
* Own worldwide launches, including operational readiness and compliance in each region
* Define the business metrics and run the business against them. These include verification pass rates, fraud losses, false positive and negative rates, seller time-to-resolution, and seller satisfaction
* Raise the bar for product management by mentoring PMs and acting as a technical product leader across SPS
A day in the life
You might start the morning with science and engineering partners looking into a spike in failed bank account verifications. Together you'd decide whether it's a new fraud pattern or friction for legitimate sellers, and how to adjust risk controls. Later you could be in a narrative review with senior leaders about a multi-year investment in the verification platform. title: Principal Product Manager, Developer Experience and Integration Platform, Amazon Freight
description:
Every shipper and platform that connects to ASCS Shipping and Freight starts the same way: an engineer reads our documentation, requests credentials, and tries to make a first successful call or EDI transmission. When that path takes weeks instead of days, shippers delay launch and revenue waits. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to make ASCS Shipping and Freight the simplest logistics provider in the industry to integrate with, across both API and EDI.
You will own the strategy and roadmap for how developers onboard and integrate with ASCS Shipping and Freight. The role spans two integration models. 1P integrations are custom, direct integrations with large shippers, where their engineering teams connect enterprise systems to our APIs or EDI. 3P integrations are platform partnerships with ecommerce platforms, fulfillment providers, multi-carrier platforms, and TMS and WMS providers, where one integration unlocks shipping for thousands of merchants. You will define a path that serves both: repeatable and self-service for platforms, and configurable without becoming bespoke engineering for large shippers.
Your charter covers four areas. First, simplify and streamline developer onboarding, from developer registration, data-access approval, and credential management through sandbox testing, certification, and go-live. Second, own the developer documentation portal as a product, including API reference, EDI implementation guides, code samples, Postman collections, and changelogs. Third, use AI to cut time to onboard and integrate, including AI assistants that answer developer questions, generate integration code and EDI mappings, diagnose failed calls, and docs that AI coding tools can consume directly. Fourth, own the integration product strategy across API and EDI, closing capability gaps between the two channels.
You will work as a peer to the Solutions Architect (SA) team, who lead hands-on technical engagements with shippers and partners, and with Support Engineering, whose support-contact data shows where developers get stuck. SAs and Support Engineering bring direct insight into where integrations stall, and you turn those patterns into product, documentation, and tooling that remove the need for the next escalation. The goal is that SAs spend their time on the most complex, highest-value launches while standard integrations complete through self-service.
This is a deeply technical role. You will review API designs, EDI transaction mappings, and authentication models with principal engineers and Solutions Architects as a peer, and you will build working calls yourself to test the experience a developer gets. You will also influence leaders across the org whose teams build the capabilities developers integrate with.
We measure success by developer outcomes: time from registration to first successful call, time from kickoff to production go-live for 1P and 3P integrations, percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service, integration completion rate, sandbox-to-production parity, API and EDI error rates, and integration-related support contacts. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
Define the strategy for developer experience and integrations across API and EDI for ASCS Shipping and Amazon Freight, and secure alignment from engineering, Solutions Architecture, business development, partnerships, and senior leadership.
Map and instrument every step of the integration journey for 1P and 3P developers and remove the largest sources of friction first: developer registration, data-access approval, and credential lifecycle, including identity verification requests, audit pauses, and credential expiry.
Own the developer docs portal as a product with owners, standards, and metrics. Deliver accurate API reference generated from OpenAPI specifications, EDI implementation guides, quick-start guides, sample code, Postman collections, and a reliable sandbox.
Define and launch AI capabilities that cut time to integrate, such as a developer assistant trained on our docs, automated EDI mapping and validation, AI-generated sample code, failed-call diagnosis, and machine-readable docs and MCP servers for AI coding tools.
Define the EDI roadmap (for example, ANSI X12 tender, status, and invoice transactions) and close capability gaps between EDI and API across business lines.
Own the percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service. Run a shared blocker list with the Solutions Architect and Support Engineering teams, prioritize fixes, and convert custom enterprise requirements into configurable, reusable capabilities, so the next large shipper launches faster than the last.
Partner with Business Development and Solutions Architects to prioritize 3P platform integrations by shipper reach. Own the technical content of partner certification, including what gets tested, the validation tooling, and the pass criteria, in support of the certification program run by Partnerships.
Own outbound communication of built and planned enhancements to 1P shippers and 3P partners, including roadmap previews, release communications, enablement, and adoption tracking. Share field-level guidance with partners only after the owning team confirms deployment.
Partner with the product leaders who own account modeling, account lifecycle, centralized KYC, and segmentation, so developer onboarding and credential approval run on the same account and identity foundations across business lines.
Own the integration funnel metrics, run voice-of-developer programs, analyze support contacts, and use the results to set priorities.
Write PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, coordinate developer communications and deprecations, and mentor product managers on technical product practice.

Each engagement is a 45-day sprint scoped on business outcomes. We leave behind systems the customer owns and keeps extending, and what we learn on every engagement goes back into AWS services.
We are looking for a Principal Product Manager - Technical to lead product across several concurrent FDE PODs. You are the Product Lead for our most complex engagements and multi-sprint programs, you develop the Product Leads who run the other PODs, and you hold executive relationships with customer CIOs and CTOs. You turn single-engagement wins into reusable capability that works across customers and industries, and you surface the next opportunities at the customers you serve. With customer executives you are an ambassador for how Amazon works, and you earn the trust that lets you hold a firm line on how the FDE team executes.
You will also build the mechanism that connects the field to the product. FDE learns things on every engagement that AWS service teams need to know. You will build and run the way the whole FDE organization feeds code, patterns and customer evidence-backed requirements back to those teams, so that customer problems get solved in the product rather than worked around on every sprint.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead product across several concurrent PODs, or one complex multi-sprint program, owning outcomes from qualification through step back for each
- Develop and coach the Product Leads on other PODs, and raise the bar for qualification, discovery, delivery and capability transfer across the organization
- Hold executive relationships at the CIO and CTO level, run executive envisioning sessions, and shape what customers choose to fund
- Surface new opportunities at existing customers and across industries, and turn them into qualified engagements with measurable outcomes
- Build and run the org-wide mechanism that feeds code, patterns and requirements from FDE PODs back to AWS service teams, and measure what it changes in the product
- Turn solutions built for one customer into reusable assets, accelerators and platform capabilities that other PODs and customers use
- Shape how agentic systems are architected across PODs, identifying trade-offs and failure modes before they appear and holding teams to a high technical bar
- Leave customers with capability. Success is the customer operating and extending the solution after the POD exits, and you set the standard for how every POD proves it
- Advocate inside AWS for the capabilities customers need, with evidence drawn from patterns across customer engagements
A day in the life
You might start the morning with a customer CTO reviewing results from the first sprint and agreeing the outcomes for the second, spend midday with a service team's product leader walking through a pattern three of your PODs have had to work around, and end the day coaching a Product Lead through a hard scope decision on their POD. title: Principal Product Manager, Technical - Amazon Freight Support Exp, Amazon Freight
description:
When a shipper moves a truckload with Amazon Freight, they expect the load to be scheduled, tracked, and delivered without having to chase anyone. Today, too much of that experience depends on manual work. Support associates switch between many tools to find information, repetitive tasks stay manual, and some work happens outside our systems where no one can see it, measure it, or automate it. Shippers feel the result as slow answers and repeat contacts. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to change that: to make shipper support for Amazon Freight fast, measurable, and increasingly automated.
You will own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, covering the platform, automation, and AI that associates use to resolve shipper issues. Your mandate has three parts. First, eliminate the reasons shippers contact us, by finding root causes in scheduling, tendering, tracking, disruptions, and billing and driving fixes upstream with the teams that own them. Second, make every piece of operational work visible and owned, by consolidating work done in other systems into a single operator console and ensuring every task has an owner, a queue, and a service level. Third, automate the work that does not need human judgment, using rule-based automation first and AI agents where they add value.
The heart of this role is a continuous automation flywheel. You will define the architecture for a framework that captures task-level data across operational workflows (what work is done, why, and how long it takes), then run a repeatable cycle of discover, document, model, measure, build, and automate. You will use that data and AI to find and rank automation candidates, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks in areas like scheduling, disruption recovery, trailer pool management, and proactive shipper communications, and route exceptions to the right operator. Every eliminated task is recorded, so the team can prove impact and reinvest the time saved.
This is a technical role. You will work with engineers on the operator platform architecture, the data model for task capture, integrations with the operational systems that work moves out of, and the design of AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions safely. You will make build-versus-reuse decisions, weigh trade-offs between rule-based and AI approaches, and set the guardrails for automation.
You will partner closely with Amazon Freight support operations leaders, who own priorities and targets for their teams, and with engineering, operations, policy, and the product teams that own scheduling, execution, and disruption management. You propose solutions backed by data; operations validates them; engineering builds them. You will work as a peer to the Amazon Shipping support product leader, sharing platforms, patterns, and AI capabilities so that what works in one business scales to the other.
We measure success with the same metrics as our other shipper support products: support contacts per load, first-contact resolution, shipper satisfaction (CSAT), automation rate, average handle time, and annual cost savings. Because measurable work comes first, you will also own input metrics that show the work is visible: share of associate work captured in the operator console, share of contacts with a recorded reason, tasks with an owner and service level, and tasks eliminated through automation. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
• Define the 3-year vision and strategy for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, and secure alignment from operations, engineering, and senior leadership across Amazon Freight and ASCS.
• Analyze contact drivers by shipper segment (enterprise, mid-market, small business) and mode, identify the root causes behind repeat and avoidable contacts, and drive fixes with the teams that own scheduling, tendering, tracking, and billing.
• Define and deliver the consolidation of support work now done outside the operator console into a single tool, so associates plan, execute, and record their work in one place. Sequence the migration in a published priority order and retire replaced shadow tools and dashboards as each workflow moves.
• Define the data model and architecture that captures 100% of associate task execution by task type, reason, and time spent, so labor is measurable by task and the business can model demand, measure productivity, and size automation.
• Define owners, queues, severity tiers, and service levels for every task type, with a daily view for managers, so no shipper issue sits open without an operator.
• Lead the discover, document, model, measure, build, automate cycle. Rank automation candidates with data and AI, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks, and use AI to propose new workflows from what the team learns.
• Define the strategy for AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions, including the guardrails, human review points, and quality measures that let associates trust them.
• Partner with operations and policy owners so standard operating procedures (SOPs) are current, structured, and usable by both associates and automation.
• Own PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, drive launches from requirements through adoption and measured impact, and mentor product managers on technical product practice.

title: Program Manager III, Integrations, Amazon Shipping
description:
Amazon Shipping delivers packages for businesses across the United States and Europe, and most of our parcels arrive through API integrations with shippers and shipping software partners such as multi-carrier platforms, warehouse and order management systems, and e-commerce platforms. Every shipper launch depends on a chain of teams landing their part on time: Solutions Architects who design the integration, the developer platform team that grants API access, Product and Engineering who build the capabilities shippers need, Partnerships who manage the software partners, and Commercial who own the shipper relationship. The External System Integrations team owns that launch experience, from a shipper's first technical conversation to go-live and the first weeks of live shipping.
Do you want to own the program that decides how fast a shipper goes from signed deal to first shipment? Have you found where months of elapsed time actually go, and taken them out? Amazon Shipping is seeking a Senior Program Manager to own the shipper integration launch program across the United States and Europe. Hundreds of shippers launch with us each year, from enterprise retailers with complex multi-system landscapes to mid-market shippers launching through existing software partners. You will define the program, break time to first shipment into stages the team can measure and improve, drive the dependencies that hold launches back, and build the capacity and peak plans leadership commits against. You will also run the mechanisms that keep a growing team out of firefighting: launch standards, post-launch handoff, error reduction, and a working relationship with every team we depend on.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the shipper launch portfolio across the United States and Europe, covering every launch from technical discovery to go-live and post-launch handoff, with a single view of stage, risk, owner and date

Messages overlap, arrive on channels the shipper does not watch, or arrive after the shipper has already called support to find out what happened. You will own the product strategy and roadmap for shipper communications, covering both what reaches shippers and what reaches the internal operators and account managers who act on their behalf. We measure success by shipper outcomes: the share of shipper-impacting disruptions where we notify the shipper before they contact support, notification delivery within the target time for each severity and audience, the share of issues where the responsible operator or account manager is alerted before the shipper escalates, the share of shippers with communication preferences set, engagement and action rates, opt-out rates, communication volume per shipper, and support contacts avoided through proactive communication. title: AIML - LLM Inference Quality Engineer
description:
Apple is building the next generation of AI data center infrastructure to power large language model (LLM) services at scale. We are looking for a senior engineer to own the correctness, consistency, and stability of LLM inference in production. You will design and build the automation frameworks, evaluation methodology, and qualification strategy that give us confidence in every model, prompt, serving stack, and infrastructure change before it reaches our users. Your work is the safety net that lets Apple ship frontier AI quickly, without sacrificing quality, safety, or trust.
In this role, you will lead the qualification of an LLM inference, output-correctness, automation framework for large-scale AI data center deployment and platform validation. You will architect qualification systems for generative AI, including agentic workflows and tool-using models, running at data center scale, validating that outputs remain correct, consistent, and stable as models, weights, prompts, serving runtimes, quantization schemes, and accelerator hardware change underneath them.
This is a hands-on AI systems engineering role at the intersection of machine learning, distributed systems, and quality engineering. You will write production-quality software in Python, C++, and/or Swift, apply statistical and ML-evaluation methods to validate both data and model behavior, and build AI-assisted QA tooling that makes testing itself smarter and faster. You will partner closely with ML engineers, inference/performance engineers, distributed systems engineers, and platform teams, and you will be a trusted Quality voice on what “correct” and “stable” mean for LLM inference at scale, including the inherently non-deterministic, probabilistic nature of generative output. You should be comfortable operating in ambiguity, defining quality bars where none exist yet, and delivering rigorous results on tight schedules.
Minimum qualifications: 1 year of experience with hardware and/or software development lifecycle processes.
1 year of experience in one or more compiled languages (e.g., C, C++, Objective-C/Swift).
Proficiency in one or more scripting languages (e.g., Python, Go, or JavaScript).
Experience using AI/LLMs to improve testing itself — test-case generation, defect detection, or reducing manual QA effort.
Familiarity with LLM serving and inference optimization (batching, KV-cache, quantization, speculative decoding, distributed/multi-accelerator serving) and GPU-accelerated software.
Experience with CI/CD, Kubernetes, containers, and cloud-native systems, and integrating automated evals into release pipelines.
Experience with machine learning and LLMs, their common practical applications, and commonly used frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, or comparable inference/serving stacks).
Experience with observability and distributed tracing for ML systems (e.g., Splunk, Prometheus, Grafana, LangSmith, or similar) and monitoring for model drift.
B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: 5+ years using one or more of the following scripting languages: Python, Go, or JavaScript
5+ years of experience working with and building operating systems
2+ years of experience in LLM testing/development.

title: Engineering Manager, Private Cloud Compute Inference Routing
description:
At Apple, iCloud Platform Engineering builds the server stack behind Push Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime, iCloud, iCloud Private Relay and Private Cloud Compute (PCC), the backbone of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead PCC inference routing. These systems send every inference request to the right compute across a global, multi-region fleet, while keeping latency low, availability high and PCC's privacy guarantees intact.
This is a technically grounded leadership role for someone who thrives at scale, can bring clarity to complex and fast-changing environments, and is energized by building both systems and teams. You'll guide architectural direction, scale operational practices and develop the engineers and leaders who will shape how Apple delivers cloud inference.
Routing LLM inference at Apple's scale takes systems that adapt to changing demand, available capacity and failures while keeping latency low and accelerator utilization high. As the fleet grows across regions and cells, routing must account for capacity and health across the whole fleet, not just a single site. PCC adds a basic architectural requirement: request content stays encrypted outside trusted compute nodes. You'll lead the design of routing and scheduling strategies within this privacy model. Together with inference and security teams, you'll evaluate techniques such as cache-aware request placement and prefill/decode disaggregation. Your scope includes the inference AI gateway layer, where requests are authenticated, metered, prioritized and streamed back to clients, all without exposing request content.
This work has broad reach. Every improvement to routing makes Siri AI and Apple Intelligence faster and more reliable, and makes better use of Apple's inference capacity. In your first year, you'll be expected to grow a high-performing organization, set a clear technical roadmap, and measurably improve routing latency, availability and fleet utilization.
Minimum qualifications: Extensive software engineering experience with a demonstrated track record of leading teams that design, build, and operate large-scale distributed systems in production environments—whether through direct management, indirect oversight, or a combination thereof
Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing engineers and leaders

Expertise of LLM inference serving, including request routing, KV-cache placement and reuse, prefill/decode disaggregation, and the tradeoffs between latency, throughput and accelerator use
A record of shipping highly reliable systems in high-availability environments, including leading incident management, on-call and reliability practices
Strong technical depth: capable of contributing meaningfully to architectural and design discussions with senior engineers, with a server development background in Java, C/C++, Go or Swift

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent professional experience
Preferred qualifications: Proven leadership in developing LLM inference serving or routing platforms (e.g., llm-d, NVIDIA Dynamo, vLLM, SGLang, or managed inference services)
Experience building or running inference AI gateways and their core behaviors: token-based rate limiting and usage metering, multi-model routing with fallback, retries and circuit breaking, and streamingresponse handling
Track record of scaling teams and organizations during rapid growth while maintaining top-tier hiring and engineering standards

description:
Looking to make a difference and shape the interface people use to manage their files on every Apple platform? Come join our collaborative, driven team!

title: Hardware Reliability Engineer – Ecosystem Accessories
description:
We are Apple’s Hardware Reliability Engineering team, and we are looking for you to work with our diverse softgoods hardware engineering teams! As the Reliability team, we are responsible for ensuring and improving the durability and reliability of Apple's products. To achieve that, we partner with multiple engineering teams from the beginning (concept) to the end (field returns) of a product lifecycle by helping to explore new technologies and understand how customers will use our products. If you have a passion for constant learning and innovative engineering products, you will fit right in. You will develop and implement creative reliability tests on new hardware programs, quantify reliability risk, support failure analysis resulting from these tests, and advise the executive team on the best path forward. Our work ensures that our products meet the rigorous expectations of our customers and survive whatever our customers can throw at them – we break things so you don’t have to. Come join our team!
Our team works specifically on Softgoods accessories and Ecosystem testing – products such as our phone cases, watch bands, and the interactions these products have with their respective systems. We work closely with the design, manufacturing, and quality teams to evaluate the performance of our products through the suite of reliability tests that we design and use these results to motivate design and process changes iteratively to ultimately deliver better products to our customers. We have a hand in every softgoods product that is released and both design the tests and analyze the test results to suite each products’ specific use cases and product definitions.
You will be responsible for ensuring our products meet the rigorous expectations of our customers and survive what life may throw at them. To do so, you will be working with cross-functional teams from concept to mass production to identify risks in the design, develop tests to evaluate the performance of the product with regards to those concerns, work with the team to understand failures, and recommend and verify the efficacy of the corresponding corrective actions. You will need to rigorously justify your tests with well characterized user behaviors and thorough understanding of field stresses, and a strong technical background to not only participate in failure analysis (FA), but also drive FA and lead the team through complex problem solving. We will push the performance of our products to the limits of the material and design, and in those cases, you will need to prepare comprehensive risk assessments to fully quantify any field exposure we may have.

title: IR Scanning Electrician
description:
In Places, we don’t sit back and let things happen, we make things happen, and we do this in service to all Apple employees and customers.
