We develop and manage Apple’s global real estate portfolio, lead all related capital construction projects, provide outstanding facilities and site services, develop and lead sustainability initiatives to reduce the environmental impact of all Apple facilities, including commute and renewable energy programs, and do everything we can to ensure the health and safety of all Apple personnel, facilities, and customers in our facilities around the world.
The Critical Facilities Electrical team is responsible for the safe and reliable operation of electrical systems and critical infrastructure across Apple's NorCal Places portfolio. We partner closely with engineering, operations, and capital projects to protect the people and work that depend on our electrical systems.
We are seeking a detail-oriented and safety-driven IR Scanning Electrician to join our team as the dedicated thermographer responsible for infrared inspections of electrical equipment across Apple's NorCal campuses. Current Level I infrared thermography qualification or certification from a recognized program aligned with an applicable industry standard or employer-approved written practice (e.g., ASNT SNT-TC-1A or equivalent).
Demonstrated experience conducting infrared inspections of energized electrical distribution equipment rated from 120/208 V through 12 kV.

Ability to work independently while following established procedures and coordinating with site operations personnel.

Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, panel schedules, and electrical drawings.
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs and work from ladders or lifts as required.

Program development: Hands-on experience establishing or scaling a predictive, condition-based infrared inspection program.
Complex electrical apparatus: In-depth experience assessing switchgear, transformers, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, automatic transfer switches (ATS), busway, and emergency/standby generation systems.
Electrical safety studies: Working familiarity with arc-flash assessments, equipment incident-energy labeling, and compliance documentation under NFPA 70E.

title: ISE, Incubation - Software Development Engineer - Proactive
description:
We are a creativity-oriented engineering team focused on conceiving and prototyping the future of software on Apple’s devices. We take big, fuzzy ideas about what might be possible and turn them into concrete concepts, prototypes and livable software! We are passionate about exploring new ideas using whatever tools help us make something tangible. Most often, we choose to modify or extend Apple’s existing software using Objective-C or Swift. But we’re open to using the best tools that help us learn: design tools, prototyping apps, ML, etc. We are looking for a creative, learning-oriented, collaborative individual to come help us explore what the future could look like.
Our team nurtures early-stage ideas into well-developed, usable experiences. For this big idea to work, is there a piece of experience that must feel great? Is there an enabling technology we need to build? Software is the tool we use most frequently to bring concepts to life on our devices. But we try to use the best tool for the job: anything that helps us see, touch, or feel an idea. We often work directly with other teams to leverage expertise from across the company, and share our work with others to find out what works and what doesn’t. Gradually, those fuzzy notions turn into tangible, brand-new ideas that can lead the future of software on our devices. The products we build are part prototype, part proof of concept and part sales pitch, so communicating clearly and being able to empathize with other people's perspectives are key skills for our team. So is the ability to give and receive feedback.

3 years experience of creative prototyping in software
Expertise in Swift or Objective-C, or equally strong experience in Python + ML stacks
Preferred qualifications: Able to deal with ambiguity, and a gut instinct for making things that will help bring clarity. We often work on projects where we need to create something to help understand the objectives & boundaries.

title: Image Quality Engineer - Camera and Photos
description:

Comprehensive understanding of end-to-end camera architectures, spanning sensor physics, lens optics, Image Signal Processors (ISP), and modern computational photography frameworks.
Superb written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to foster collaboration across multidisciplinary hardware, software, and creative teams.

title: Silicon Debug Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for solving the hardest problems in silicon? Do you thrive at the intersection of circuit theory, device physics, and hands-on failure investigation? As part of our Silicon Debug group, you'll take complex, often elusive silicon failures and systematically uncover their root cause — from electrical characterization all the way down to physical analysis. You and your team will apply deep engineering fundamentals and cutting-edge failure analysis techniques to enable product ramp at scale. Your efforts will directly impact the quality and reliability of state-of-the-art ASICs that power experiences for millions of customers worldwide. Join us, and you'll play a central role in ensuring the silicon we build is everything it needs to be.
We have an extraordinary opportunity for Silicon Debug Engineers to investigate and root-cause failures in advanced custom digital megacells (SRAM memories, on-chip sensors, custom data paths) used in high-performance, low-power SoCs. You will bridge the gap between electrical debug and physical failure analysis, working at the frontier of silicon investigation.
Imagine yourself at the center of our SoC bring-up and product ramp effort, collaborating across circuit design, process engineering, DFT, and failure analysis teams — with a critical impact on getting functional products to millions of customers quickly.
Minimum qualifications: A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience in one or more of the following areas: SRAM circuits, custom circuit design, silicon debug.
Experience in design or debug of low-voltage / low-power custom circuits.
Deep understanding of deep-submicron device physics, leakage mechanisms, and technology interactions with device behavior.
Solid understanding of device matching, device noise sources (1/f, thermal), extrinsic noise sources (supply noise, jitter), and their impact on high-precision circuits.
Familiarity with electrical failure analysis (eFA) techniques and physical failure analysis (pFA) workflows, and the ability to plan FA strategies based on electrical debug data.
Understanding of Dynamic Lock-in Thermography (DLS) and Lock-in Thermography (LIT) for localization of resistive and leakage defects, including their sensitivity limits and how thermal signatures correlate to specific circuit fault modes.
Knowledge of Nanoprobe techniques for electrical probing of deep-submicron nodes, and appreciation of how probe contact, voltage bias, and electron beam exposure can perturb sensitive analog or memory circuits.
Awareness of how physical sample preparation steps (deprocessing, FIB cross-section, delayering) can alter or destroy evidence of electrical failures, and how to coordinate FA plans that preserve failure signatures.
Ability to interpret FA results (photon emission maps, OBIRCH, thermal maps, TEM/SEM imagery) in the context of circuit topology and failure electrical signatures.
Ability to conduct structured experiments during silicon debug, gather and analyze large datasets, and utilize scripting to support efficient handling of debug data.
Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Perl, or others) and CAD automation tools.
Knowledge of industry-standard circuit design and simulation tools.

title: Sr. Software Engineer (Observability Solutions) - Enterprise Technology Services
description:

12+ years of experience with OOP languages such as Java, Go, etc. with production experience building backend services or infrastructure components.
Solid experience designing and operating components of distributed systems — including replication, fault tolerance, and distributed coordination.
Hands-on experience contributing to systems that handle large-scale or petabyte-scale data workloads.

12+ years of overall experience.

title: Wireless Intelligence Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:
Are you excited by the idea of wireless devices that can sense, learn and adapt on their own? Do you enjoy problems where real-time embedded systems meet machine learning? In the Wireless Technologies and Ecosystems (WTE) organization, you'll help bring smart, reliable connectivity to the world through cellular, satellite and Wi-Fi. Our team builds the intelligence behind that connectivity: the scheduling control software that runs on various Apple products, and ML-driven schedulers and models that power wireless intelligence features. You'll design, develop and deliver the next generation of these technologies so that connections stay fast, robust and power-efficient.
Join WTE and be part of a world-class team of engineers working with cross-functional partners to drive innovation in products used by millions of people worldwide. We are looking for talented, highly motivated, self-directed engineers who can work across layers, from embedded scheduling and control software to the ML models that guide it. Our work starts on Apple Watch and extends to iPhone, iPad, Mac and other wireless products, solving everyday connectivity problems at scale. You'll take ideas from research and prototype through to shipping features, and your work will directly shape how Apple products connect.
We are looking for a highly motivated software engineer to join an exceptional development team building wireless intelligence for Apple's next-generation products. In this role, you will develop wireless software solutions used across Apple’s wireless products, combining embedded software development with applied artificial intelligence and machine learning. Your work will include designing ML-driven smart scheduling algorithms for 5G/6G, satellite and Wi-Fi, and integrating them into real-time, resource-constrained embedded systems. You'll take ownership of features end to end, from prototyping and evaluation through production integration, validation and field performance analysis. The role needs exceptional problem-solving and communication skills, strong programming ability, careful attention to detail and a passion for building great products. This position demands exceptional problem-solving and communication abilities, robust programming proficiency, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passionate commitment to creating superior products. You will do well in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, and your contributions will make a clear difference to future Apple products.
Minimum qualifications: MSc in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
Strong foundation in wireless communication systems, such as 5G NR/LTE, Wi-Fi (802.11) or satellite communications.
Hands-on experience developing and applying machine learning models to engineering problems.
Proficiency in C/C++ and Python.
Experience using AI coding tools as part of your regular workflow, with the ability to critically review, verify and debug AI-generated code.
Preferred qualifications: PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
Experience with embedded or real-time software development on resource-constrained devices.
Knowledge of MAC/PHY scheduling, radio resource management, or multi-radio coexistence.
Experience deploying ML models on-device, model quantization and optimization.

Track record of taking research concepts or prototypes through to product-quality implementations.
Ability to communicate complex technical work clearly to cross-functional partners and senior engineers.

title: Customer Support
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As part of our Member Experience team, you will play a vital role in delivering unparalleled support, working directly with customers to provide a world-class experience. You will be the voice and advocate of our brand, ensuring every interaction leaves a lasting impression of trust, satisfaction, and delight. By actively addressing customer needs and exceeding their expectations, you will contribute not only to the success of our customers but also to the growth and reputation of our company. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop real-world expertise in customer service, creative problem-solving, and impactful communication, all while making a tangible difference in the lives of our customers and the future of Base. 

 

What You'll Do

 - Engage with members across phone, email, text, and other communication channels, delivering personalized and delightful experiences that leave a lasting impact.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve member issues related to Base Power's innovative products, ensuring seamless and satisfying solutions.

 - Utilize tools to track, manage, troubleshoot, and prioritize member interactions, ensuring every concern is addressed promptly and efficiently.

 - Partner with engineering, marketing, and operations teams to streamline processes, enhance the member experience, and drive continuous improvement.

 - Act as the “voice of the customer”, gathering valuable feedback and insights to shape the future of our products and services.

 - Create and maintain detailed documentation, knowledge bases, playbooks, and team resources to ensure consistency in service.

 - Support new members during onboarding to ensure they understand and can fully utilize Base Power's products from the start.
   
    

What You'll Bring

 - Graduation year between 2025-2027.

 - Empathetic communicator who loves connecting with people and making them feel heard.

 - Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity.

 - Ability to think analytically and creatively to resolve complex issues and suggest process improvements.

 - Attention to detail in communicating accurately and clearly, tracking customer interactions, and documenting solutions.

 - Skilled at managing multiple tasks and inquiries simultaneously while meeting deadlines and response time goals.

 - Natural inclination to stay calm under pressure and step up to proactively de-escalate frustrating situations.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes while maintaining high-quality support.

 - Tech savvy, with a knack for quickly mastering new tools and systems.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company’s best interests first.

 

About the Team

The Member Experience team is the face of Base to our members—and the voice of our members back to Base. We’re deeply customer-obsessed and uniquely cross-functional, with a strong understanding of what every team does and how it all connects. By seeing firsthand what’s working well and what should be improved, we surface insights that help inform what the business builds and prioritizes next. Every day brings a new challenge, balancing high ownership and accountability with constant collaboration and support from the team.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

As part of our Member Experience team, you will own quality assurance and training for our frontline support team. You'll make sure every member who reaches out to Base gets accurate, clear, and empathetic help, no matter who picks up. This role blends program ownership with hands-on coaching. You'll build the scorecards, curriculum, and feedback loops that help new agents ramp quickly and help tenured agents keep getting better. You will use data, member feedback, and direct observation to find what's working and fix what isn't, so quality holds up as our member base grows.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Quality assurance scorecard – Build and maintain rubrics across phone, email, chat, and text that measure accuracy, empathy, and resolution.

 - Interaction reviews – Build and maintain a structured program for you and team leads to review a consistent sample of member interactions for every agent every week, leveraging AI to build systems as needed.

 - Calibration – Run regular calibration sessions with team leads and others, so every reviewer grades to the same standard. Manage the process for agents to ask questions about or dispute their scores.

 - Coaching and feedback – Turn QA results into agent-shareable scores and specific, actionable coaching feedback. Partner with team leads on 1:1s and performance improvement plans, and give agents clear, kind feedback they can act on.

 - New hire onboarding – Design and run training for new agents, from classroom learning to shadowing to nesting to self-sufficiency. Set clear ramp milestones and certify agents before they work independently.

 - Ongoing training – Build continuing education for the whole team: refreshers, product and policy updates, and advanced skills like de-escalation and handling hard conversations. Track completion and measure whether training changes results.

 - Knowledge management – Keep the knowledge base, standard operating procedures (SOPs), call guides, and saved reply templates accurate and current. Make sure agents always know where to find the right answer.

 - Metrics and reporting – Track and report on QA scores, member satisfaction (CSAT), first contact resolution (FCR), and new hire ramp time. Connect QA findings to member outcomes and share trends with leadership.

 - Root cause analysis – Find patterns in QA results and member feedback. Separate training gaps from process, tooling, and product issues, and drive the fix at the source.

 - Compliance and risk – Make sure agents follow policies on contracts, billing, and disclosures. Flag risks early and escalate them to Legal and Finance.

 - Voice of the member – Share what you see in member interactions to help shape better experiences, services, and policies across the company.

 - Launch readiness – Partner with other teams so agents are trained and ready before new policies, features, and launches reach members.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2-8+ years of experience in quality assurance, training, or enablement for a customer support, contact center, or customer success team.

 - Hands-on experience building QA scorecards, running calibration sessions, and turning review results into coaching plans.

 - Experience designing and delivering training, including new hire onboarding and ongoing skill development.

 - Coaching skills that change behavior: direct, kind, and specific feedback that agents trust.

 - Comfort with data. You can analyze QA scores, CSAT, FCR, and NPS, then turn what you find into clear recommendations.

 - Comfort owning outcomes end-to-end, as motivated to fix the root cause as to improve the individual interaction.

 - Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity for training materials, SOPs, and feedback.

 - Confidence facilitating, from 1:1 coaching sessions to full-team trainings.

 - Tech savvy, with experience in help desk platforms, QA tools, learning management systems, and knowledge bases, and a knack for quickly mastering new ones.

 - Not afraid to get on the front line. You'll listen to calls, read tickets, and take contacts yourself to understand what agents face.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company's best interests first.

Founded in 2017 with dual headquarters in Chicago and Tokyo, CADDi serves manufacturing leaders across more than 20 countries. We recently announced a $114M Series D funding round at a $1.2B valuation, bringing total funding to $234M, backed by top-tier investors including Salesforce Ventures, Woven Capital, and Atomico.
We are expanding our North American operations rapidly and building next-generation products like CADDi Explorer and CADDi Agent. If you are eager to solve hard data and engineering problems while scaling a fast-growing unicorn, we’d love to talk.

As a Deployment Partner, you own a customer from first discovery through a live, adopted workflow, and then through expansion across the enterprise. You work directly with the people who run the plant floor, procurement, quality, and engineering from operational management up to the C-suite deciding where AI fits in their business.
You work with the CADDi AI Data Platform and suite of workflow-specific products a configurable tool you capitalize on for each customer. You are accountable for their success end-to-end: time-to-value, the deployment of the solutions we promised, the measurable value they see enterprise-wide, and the renewal that follows.
The role folds pre-sales, customer success, and data expertise into a single owner, working alongside an Account Executive on the commercial side and Forward Deployed Engineers who build the technical pieces beyond what you configure.

Understand the customer
Deployment Partners take the deepest, most strategic accounts, leading value validation, designing the technical solution, orchestrating Forward Deployed Engineers, and driving change at the executive level.
Meet with cross-functional teams across engineering, procurement, quality, and operations onsite as needed to learn how they work and where time and money are lost.
Advise customer leaders, from operational management to the C-suite, on where AI and a shared data foundation create the most value, and agree on what success means for their business.
Identify the data that matters (drawings, quotes, part records, supplier data) and model it into the platform, working with Forward Deployed Engineers where deeper integration is needed.
Partner with Sales before the deal closes to validate value with real customer data and show an early, concrete win. Build and deliver tailored demos for prospects and existing customers.
Deploy and drive adoption
Own the deployment plan from scoping to production, coordinating customer stakeholders across business units, IT, procurement, and compliance.
Define the semantic layer for the customer’s data, configure the data layer, and build the Explorer configuration and plugins the deployment needs, reusing existing configurations, plugins, and libraries wherever possible to move fast.
Deploy CADDi’s workflow products for each user group and shape deployments of CADDi Agent, run training and adoption sessions
Orchestrate Forward Deployed Engineers on the technical gap between the standard platform and what the customer needs, such as data pipelines, custom integrations, and advanced analytics.
Define the success metrics and quality bar for each deployment, track them, and run QBRs to customer and CADDi leadership.
Own operations after go-live and grow the account
Own the operational health of every live deployment, so environments, data pipelines, configurations, and access stay reliable as the customer’s data, users, and processes change
Design and quantify ROI, and present findings to audiences from shop-floor users to the executive team to drive decisions and action.
Identify expansion opportunities within accounts and work with the Account Executive to turn them into new business, including upsell, cross-sell, and global rollout.
Bring what you see in the field back to Product and Engineering so it shapes the roadmap, and return reusable configurations and learnings to the shared library so the next deployment is faster.

Curiosity and ownership: you keep digging past the first answer, and you follow through on every one of several complex, visible projects at once.
Comfort with ambiguity: you do your best work in messy, unstructured customer environments, and you know when to lead and when to support.
Bias for speed: you would rather put something real in front of users this week than something perfect next quarter.

8+ years in a customer-facing technical role (solutions consulting, implementation, forward-deployed engineering, analytics consulting, or similar), with a track record of owning complex deployments end-to-end and driving measurable adoption and expansion.
Strong written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences, from operational management up to the C-suite.

description:
Company
Cox Automotive - USA
Job Family Group
Engineering / Product Development
Job Profile
AVP, Architecture
Management Level
Assistant Vice Presidents (AVP)

Hybrid - Ability to work remotely part of the week
Travel %
Yes, 15% of the time

Day
Compensation
Compensation includes a base salary in the range of $217,400.00 - $362,300.00. The base salary may vary within the anticipated base pay range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, and abilities. Position may be eligible for additional compensation that may include an incentive program.
Job Description
The AVP, Architecture (Retail Solutions) provides executive-level leadership over the architecture function for the Retail portfolio within Cox Automotive. This role is accountable for defining and executing the Retail portfolio technology strategy, driving solution and technical architecture across retail-facing value streams, and ensuring alignment with enterprise technology standards and governance. The AVP leads a team of Solution Architects and Technical Architects who design and evolve the platforms, capabilities, and integrations that power Cox Automotive's retail dealer and consumer experiences.
This leader partners closely with Retail portfolio product and engineering leadership, Enterprise Architecture, and cross-functional stakeholders to connect retail solutions to the broader Vehicle Lifecycle vision, lower cost to build through platform reuse, and embed AI capabilities into retail products.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership
Define and own the Retail Portfolio Technology Strategy, including platform capabilities, adoption goals per product, and value stream architecture roadmaps.
Oversee the entirety of architectural design, investment planning, development, and implementation for the Retail portfolio.
Establish long-range strategic direction and roadmaps for the current state and evolution of retail technology infrastructure, including dealer-facing and consumer-facing platforms.
Drive the rationalization of duplicate platforms within the Retail portfolio, setting adoption targets and retirement timelines aligned with enterprise goals.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture to ensure Retail strategies operate within enterprise guardrails while optimizing for portfolio-specific outcomes.
Architecture and Design
Lead the architecture of key Retail portfolio capabilities, including: Dealer & Partner Organization Management, Common Dealer Experience (Command Center), Retail Dealer Reporting Platform, Consumer Management (Connected Customer), Retail 3rd Party Data Curation, Dealer Communications, R360 Workflow Strategy/Governance, Retail Agentic Platform (Journey State, Context, Ontology, Tools Catalog, UX, Policies/Governance), and Retail Deal (DealXG, Payment Services).
Direct the design and development of technology products, services, standards, and best practices for retail solutions.
Ensure designs are consistent with enterprise implementation standards and in conformance with network, capacity, security, and data governance plans.
Evaluate and consult with leaders on technical operations, strategic planning of architecture, system operations, and product development, configuration, and deployment.
Governance and Standards
Define and enforce Portfolio-level policies and standards that operate within Enterprise Architecture guardrails.
Participate in the Architecture Council to support strategy cascade, standards alignment, exception management, and scorecard reporting.
Escalate enterprise-level exceptions through proper governance channels.
Oversee adoption tracking and compliance within the Retail portfolio against both enterprise and portfolio standards.
Team Leadership and Talent Development
Lead and develop a team of Value Stream Architects, Solution Architects, and Technical Architects aligned to Retail release trains.
Raise architecture capability through the engineering skills framework; mentor and coach architecture talent.
Ensure every value stream has a named architecture lead; manage quarterly capacity rebalancing.
Maintain program-level and executive sponsorship responsibility for all Retail Architecture initiatives.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with Enterprise Architecture on large, multi-stream initiatives and cross-portfolio integration design.
Collaborate with the CISO on security architecture and the CDO on data strategy for retail platforms.
Work with business leaders, legal, and other stakeholders to define data, infrastructure, and related governance standards.
Drive AI adoption within retail products in alignment with the enterprise AI risk framework and shared AI capabilities.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field with 14+ years of relevant experience, including at least 7 years in a leadership role. Or, an equivalent combination of education and work-related experience.
Master’s degree with 12+ years of relevant experience, including leadership experience, may be substituted.
Preferred
Experience in automotive retail technology, dealer management systems, or consumer digital platforms.
Deep expertise in enterprise and solution architecture, including cloud-native design, API-first strategies, and platform modernization.
Proven track record of leading large-scale platform rationalization and technology consolidation efforts.
Experience with AI/ML integration into product architectures and agentic platform design.
Strong understanding of data governance, integration patterns, and security architecture.
Functional Skills (Mastery Level)
Analytical Thinking: Applies advanced analytical techniques to complex organizational and architectural challenges.
Quality Management: Drives quality management practices across architecture teams and deliverables.
Requirements Analysis: Leads enterprise-level requirements elicitation and translates business needs into architectural solutions.
System and Technology Integration: Expert in system integration across applications, databases, and platforms at enterprise scale.
Technology Savvy: Directs evaluation and incorporation of emerging technologies, including AI, cloud, and data platforms.
Foundational Skills (Mastery Level)
Builds Partnerships: Maintains executive-level relationships across business, technology, and external partners.
Communicates with Impact: Influences senior leadership through compelling strategic narratives.
Drives Innovation: Champions innovative architectural approaches and emerging technology adoption.
Inspires Others: Motivates architecture teams toward high performance and professional growth.
Leads with Vision: Articulates a clear vision for retail technology architecture aligned with corporate strategy.
Drug Testing
To be employed in this role, you’ll need to clear a pre-employment drug test. Cox Automotive does not currently administer a pre-employment drug test for marijuana for this position. However, we are a drug-free workplace, so the possession, use or being under the influence of drugs illegal under federal or state law during work hours, on company property and/or in company vehicles is prohibited.
Benefits
The Company offers eligible employees the flexibility to take as much vacation with pay as they deem consistent with their duties, the company’s needs, and its obligations; seven paid holidays throughout the calendar year; and up to 160 hours of paid wellness annually for their own wellness or that of family members. Employees are also eligible for additional paid time off in the form of bereavement leave, time off to vote, jury duty leave, volunteer time off, military leave, and parental leave.
About Us
Through groundbreaking technology and a commitment to stellar experiences for drivers and dealers alike, Cox Automotive employees are transforming the way the world buys, owns, sells – or simply uses – cars. Cox Automotive employees get to work on iconic consumer brands like Autotrader and Kelley Blue Book and industry-leading dealer-facing companies like vAuto and Manheim, all while enjoying the people-centered atmosphere that is central to our life at Cox. Cox Fleet keeps your fleet moving!
As a Cox Automotive business, Cox Fleet delivers integrated uptime solutions designed to reduce downtime, improve fleet performance, and keep drivers safely on the road. Our nationwide operation combines more than 1,500 skilled technicians, 30+ company-operated service centers, and a network of over 65,000 service providers, all supported by 24/7/365 operational coordination. Together, we provide maintenance, repair, and fleet support services for equipment ranging from Class 8 trucks and 53-foot trailers to light-duty vehicles.
Cox Fleet is currently hiring a Lead Mobile Diesel/Trailer Technician. The Lead Mobile Diesel and Trailer Technician serves in a dual-role capacity, balancing master-level technical responsibilities in the field with operational support duties and technical leadership skills development. This role is designed for high-performing technicians who aspire to grow into future leadership or operational positions while continuing to serve as a critical technical resource for the team. In addition to performing advanced diagnostics, complex repairs, DOT inspections, and preventive maintenance, the Lead Mobile and Trailer Diesel Technician partners closely with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to support quality control inspections, technician technical coaching and development, Cox Fleet PM and telematics compliance, inventory and parts reconciliation, estimate workflows, customer engagement, and other operational initiatives that drive market performance, efficiency, safety, and operational excellence. The Lead Mobile Diesel and Trailer Technician also participates in a structured leadership development program, gaining hands-on training in people leadership, business operations, and performance management while serving as a key pipeline for future operational and leadership opportunities.
OPERATIONAL DUTIES:
Partner with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to support market-level operational initiatives designed and directed by the MTM to improve team performance, productivity, efficiency, safety, and customer satisfaction
Support technician onboarding and development efforts by demonstrating and training on company processes, workflows, safety standards, and operational best practices.
Participate in customer meetings, operational reviews, and account support activities, serving as a technical and operational representative of Cox Fleet when appropriate.
Support the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) in conducting Quality Control Inspections (QCIs) and share technical observation on repair quality, workmanship, and compliance on work completed by Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. Provide coaching and training to technicians, at the MTMs direction.
Provide guidance and support to Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr with inventory management best practices, inventory reconciliation activities, and proper tracking of parts, tools, and service truck inventories to ensure accuracy and operational efficiency
Support PM and telematics compliance initiatives within the team by working closely with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to maintain fleet readiness and ensure compliance with company standards.
Provide technical mentorship, knowledge sharing, and skill support to Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. and also Entry-Level Apprentices, in coordination with the MTM to help drive technical skill progression.
Model established workflows and best practices expected of the Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. and also Entry-Level Apprentices, along with bringing opportunities to the MTM around process improvement opportunities that enhance service quality, technician effectiveness, and overall market performance.
Provide the MTM and support teams with technical and field information that assists with scheduling, workflow coordination, and service execution.
Participate in a structured leadership-readiness program covering leadership principles, business operations, performance-coaching concepts, and process improvement in preparation for potential future leadership opportunities.
MECHANICAL DUTIES:
Diagnose, adjust and repair various types of truck equipment, including but not limited to: electrical/brake/cooling systems, starters/alternators, AC systems, fan clutches, engine electronics, diesel steering systems, gas and diesel engines, manual and automatic transmissions, clutches, differentials, etc.
Perform scheduled preventative maintenance inspections (“PMIs”), DOT Inspections and follow up repairs on light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles in a mobile/field environment.
Use hand tools, precision instruments, lift and jacks, welding equipment, diagnostic tools, technology and testing equipment, such as handheld computers and pressure gauges, to inspect, test and troubleshoot vehicle systems.
Road test vehicles to identify issues, verify repairs and ensure they are operating safely and properly.
Document completed work (including required DOT forms and service documentation), parts used and repair order findings accurately and on time using company-issued hand-held device.
Follow an assigned daily schedule with a degree of independence, effectively managing multiple concurrent tasks while exercising sound judgment to prioritize work activities and allocate time efficiently in accordance with established procedures and guidelines
Maintain a high level of productivity and be able to work within or beat most Standard Repair Times.
Serve as a senior peer technical resource for technicians by supporting advanced diagnostic efforts, assisting with complex equipment failures, and developing effective repair strategies for challenging maintenance and repair situations
Provide technical mentorship to Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr by providing hands-on coaching, technical guidance, and best practices that improve diagnostic accuracy, repair quality, productivity, and the ability to consistently perform work within or near established Standard Repair Times
Communicate with management and support team via email or phone to obtain approvals on repair estimates, retrieve purchase order numbers and/or discuss RO findings notes
Serve as a trusted partner to customers by understanding their needs, providing expert guidance and periodic updates, assist in resolving technical issues in the field and delivering a positive service experience.
Manage service truck inventory and equipment assets, including sourcing parts from approved local and national vendors, maintaining appropriate stock levels, and performing periodic inventory reconciliation to support efficient and timely repairs.
Maintain and operate a company-issued service truck and telematics unit, including managing parts and vehicle equipment, and performing inventory reconciliation.

Crowe is seeking an experienced Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) Manager to join our global cyber investigations team. This is a hands-on technical leadership role focused on incident response execution, technical quality, and team development. Primary client relationship management, sales activities, and engagement financial management are outside the scope of this position.
Key Responsibilities
Lead end-to-end incident response activities involving ransomware, data breaches, business email compromise, insider threats, intellectual property theft, and unauthorized access.
Direct incident triage, investigation, containment, eradication, recovery validation, and post-incident reporting.
Develop and recommend containment and remediation strategies to eliminate attacker access, prevent further compromise, and support safe recovery of affected environments.
Manage multiple technical response workstreams, establish priorities, assign responsibilities, coordinate resources, and adjust response strategies as new information emerges.
Serve as a senior technical escalation point, troubleshooting complex incidents, validating investigative hypotheses, and guiding responders through incomplete or conflicting evidence.
Investigate and respond to cloud, identity, email, and SaaS security incidents across Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Azure, AWS, Google Workspace, and other enterprise platforms.
Perform and oversee hands-on forensic analysis, including endpoint and memory forensics, evidence collection, timeline reconstruction, log correlation, network forensics, malware triage, and root-cause analysis.
Analyze endpoint, network, cloud, identity, and security telemetry to identify attacker activity, lateral movement, persistence mechanisms, and potential data exfiltration.
Apply threat intelligence, malware findings, and MITRE ATT&CK techniques to guide incident scoping, threat hunting, containment, and detection improvements.
Lead remote evidence collection, rapid triage, and enterprise-scale response activities across geographically distributed environments.
Ensure response activities and technical findings meet forensic evidence preservation, chain-of-custody, documentation, and quality standards.
Develop and improve incident response playbooks, runbooks, automation, detection logic, investigative methodologies, and technical reporting templates.
Supervise, mentor, and develop incident responders and forensic professionals through technical coaching, quality reviews, and performance feedback.
Communicate incident status, investigative findings, risks, limitations, and recommended actions to technical teams, executives, legal counsel, and other stakeholders.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
8+ years of experience in incident response, digital forensics, cyber investigations, or closely related cybersecurity disciplines.
2+ years of experience supervising, mentoring, or technically leading incident response, digital forensics, threat-hunting, or related cybersecurity professionals.
Demonstrated experience leading significant cybersecurity incidents and coordinating multiple technical response workstreams under tight deadlines.
Advanced hands-on expertise in incident triage, containment, eradication, endpoint and memory forensics, evidence collection, timeline analysis, log correlation, and compromise scoping.
Strong knowledge of Windows and Linux forensic analysis, including event logs, registry artifacts, file-system metadata, execution artifacts, and persistence mechanisms.
Experience investigating and responding to cloud, identity, email, and SaaS security incidents involving Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Azure, AWS, or Google Workspace.
Experience analyzing network traffic and security telemetry, including packet captures, DNS, proxy, firewall, VPN, authentication, and flow data.
Ability to independently evaluate evidence, develop and test investigative hypotheses, identify analytical gaps, and make informed response decisions under pressure.
Working knowledge of recognized incident response methodologies, including NIST SP 800-61 and/or SANS incident-handling frameworks, and practical application of MITRE ATT&CK.
Experience using incident response, forensic, endpoint detection, SIEM, and security tools such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Velociraptor, KAPE, Volatility, EnCase, FTK, Magnet AXIOM, or X-Ways.
Strong understanding of evidence preservation, chain of custody, forensic documentation, and defensible investigative reporting.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical findings and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to prioritize response activities, coordinate technical resources, and maintain analytical rigor during high-severity incidents.
Preferred Qualifications
Professional certifications such as GCIH, GCFA, GCFE, GNFA, EnCE, CFCE, CISSP, or equivalent credentials.
Experience working in a 24/7, on-call, or globally coordinated incident response environment.
Experience with enterprise threat hunting, EDR telemetry analysis, detection engineering, and developing monitoring or detection logic.
Experience developing and executing incident response playbooks, tabletop exercises, and cybersecurity readiness assessments.
Proficiency with Python, PowerShell, or similar scripting languages for forensic analysis, incident response automation, and investigative efficiency.
Experience with specialized investigations involving mobile devices, payment-card environments, eCommerce systems, web servers, or containers.
Advanced malware analysis experience beyond basic triage.
Experience supporting litigation, regulatory investigations, expert reporting, or testimony.

Successful candidates will demonstrate the ability to lead complex cybersecurity incidents, make timely and informed containment decisions, and maintain hands-on technical expertise throughout the incident response lifecycle.

About the Team
The Dasher & Logistics team ensures every delivery is completed with speed, accuracy, and a positive experience for consumers, merchants, and Dashers. We own the health of DoorDash’s delivery network, including supply and demand, cost and quality, Dasher pay and incentives, Dasher acquisition and retention, assignment and batching, and real-time operations.
Within Strategy & Operations, Dasher & Logistics is made up of teams that each own part of this system, such as Network Strategy, US Markets, Regulated Markets, Canada, Supply, Pay & Efficiency, and Live Ops. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Marketing, and Operations to run and improve one of the largest last-mile logistics networks in the world.
About the Role
We’re hiring a Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations to own a meaningful part of the Dasher & Logistics network end-to-end. Depending on the team, that could be how we invest in Dasher supply, the health of every US market, our most complex regulated markets, or the delivery network for an entire country. You will be accountable for the cost-to-quality tradeoff in your area: faster, more reliable deliveries at the same cost, or the same quality at a lower cost.
You will find where the network underperforms, design and test the fix, and work with Product and Engineering to build it into how the network runs. You will make tradeoff decisions across Dasher earnings, consumer experience, merchant reliability, and unit economics, and bring clear recommendations to senior leadership. You will also build and develop a team that can take on more over time.
Success in this role means consistently delivering a faster, more reliable delivery experience while improving cost efficiency, and making changes that last because they are built into our products and operating rhythm.
You will report into a Director or Senior Director on our Dasher & Logistics team within Strategy & Operations. We expect this role to be hybrid, with some time in-office and some time remote.

Design and run experiments that lead to clear decisions, then scale what works across markets
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Analytics to turn manual wins into durable product and system changes
Make thoughtful tradeoff decisions between cost, growth, and customer experience to protect long-term marketplace health
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, and grow the next set of leaders at DoorDash
Help keep the network running smoothly during incidents, severe weather, and holidays alongside our Live Ops partners
We’re excited about you because…

You have managed and developed high-performing teams

title: Senior Manager, Robot Operations
description:
About the Role
As Senior Manager, Robot Operations , you will lead the day-to-day execution of Dot's autonomous delivery operations in the Phoenix area, ensuring safe, reliable, high-quality, and cost-efficient performance. You will own operational outcomes across fleet availability, productivity, service quality, and unit economics while building the processes and frontline capabilities required to scale commercial operations.
This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of commercial execution and robotics R&D. Beyond running daily operations, you will partner closely with Engineering and Product teams to translate field observations, operational data, and recurring robot issues into actionable feedback that improves robot performance and reliability. You will establish a culture of ownership, operational discipline, and continuous improvement—ensuring that commercial operations deliver for customers today while accelerating the development of better robots for tomorrow.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Execute Commercial Operations: Own daily operations in Phoenix, ensuring consistent execution across robot deployment, dispatch, delivery completion, fleet readiness, and field support.
Drive Operational Performance: Deliver against key metrics for safety, availability, productivity, delivery quality, reliability, customer experience, and cost per delivery.
Build Operational Discipline: Establish and continuously improve SOPs, daily operating rhythms, performance reviews, escalation mechanisms, and frontline accountability.
Optimize Fleet Performance: Monitor robot health, utilization, downtime, intervention rates, and mission success; identify bottlenecks and drive corrective actions.
Own Cost and Productivity: Optimize staffing, fleet utilization, field support, maintenance, and other operating expenses to improve unit economics without compromising safety or quality.
Lead Frontline Teams: Build, coach, and develop a high-performing operations team; establish clear ownership, performance expectations, and a culture of hands-on execution.
Support R&D Operations: Partner with Engineering, Product, Autonomy, Hardware, and Remote Assistance teams to support field testing, software releases, hardware validation, and operational experiments.
Build the Engineering Feedback Loop: Systematically capture field issues, categorize failure modes, quantify operational impact, and drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions with Engineering and Product.
Improve Robot Reliability: Use operational data and frontline observations to identify recurring failures, reduce human interventions, improve mean time to recovery, and increase successful autonomous mission completion.
Manage Operational Readiness: Ensure robots, people, processes, and infrastructure are ready for new releases, experiments, and changes to commercial operations.
Own Incident Response: Lead operational escalations, coordinate incident resolution, ensure timely communication, and drive lessons learned into preventive actions.
Scale What Works: Develop repeatable operating mechanisms and best practices that can be standardized and replicated across future markets.

Demonstrated success leading hands-on, day-to-day operations with accountability for service delivery, operational quality, reliability, and cost.
Experience operating autonomous robots, autonomous vehicles.
Strong track record of building operational discipline, improving productivity, and delivering measurable performance improvements.
Experience managing frontline teams, workforce planning, operational processes, and performance management.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use operational data to identify trends, diagnose issues, and drive corrective actions.
Ability to work closely with technical teams to translate field problems into structured engineering feedback and measurable product improvements.
Demonstrated ownership, urgency, and sound judgment in dynamic environments where priorities can change quickly.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners and drive issues to resolution.
Willingness to be present in the field, engage directly with frontline teams, and personally troubleshoot operational challenges.
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.

Experience launching, scaling, or optimizing commercial delivery or fleet operations.
Familiarity with remote assistance, robot telemetry, fleet management systems, hardware diagnostics, and autonomy-related workflows.
Experience supporting R&D, field testing, product launches, and engineering validation in live operating environments.
Experience building structured incident management, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement programs.
Familiarity with SQL, BI dashboards, and data-driven operational performance management.
Experience improving unit economics through fleet utilization, labor productivity, maintenance optimization, and process standardization.

title: DIRECTOR OF MARKETING – YALE & AUGUST
description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.
We are building a company that is determined to win, and we are clear about how: strong brands, great people, and disciplined execution.
You'll join a team that puts customers first, keeps its commitments, and cuts through complexity to deliver meaningful results.
If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and help shape what's next for our iconic brands, we'd love to meet you. Apply now.
Explore life at Fortune Brands here .
Are you a marketing leader who can turn a trusted household name into the most-loved brand in the smart home category? The Connected Products Security team at Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Director of Marketing for our Yale and August smart lock brands , sold to consumers and to Pro and B2B customers across the US and Canada. Yale and August are trusted names on the door; this leader will make them the brands people choose first, talk about, and stay loyal to.
The Director of Marketing leads marketing for Yale and August across consumer and Pro/B2B channels, reporting to the General Manager of Connected Security. Every responsibility below spans both. We are looking for a growth-minded, data driven brand builder and operator: someone who pairs creative ambition with rigorous measurement, sets clear OKRs, and is equally strong at planning and optimizing a direct media budget, at finding new and unconventional ways to earn attention and customers, and at building product marketing for B2B and Pro channels, where installers, dealers and property managers buy differently from consumers. The Director leads a small team and a group of agency partners, owns the marketing budget, and is accountable for three outcomes: Pro and B2B activation, winning in ecomm and on shelf, and building brand leadership and growing share for Yale and August. The team operates like a startup inside a large company, so the role combines strategy with hands-on execution and you have to be a player coach. The Director will test new channels, formats and partnerships ahead of the category, and will build an agentic marketing team that lets a small group operate at the scale of a much larger one.
POSITION LOCATION:
This position can be based at our global headquarters in Deerfield, Illinois, in San Francisco, California, or remote within the United States.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategy, Brand & Team
Set a bold growth strategy, plan and budget for Yale and August, with clear OKRs for revenue, share, activation and brand health, and a clear point of view on where the next wave of customers and revenue will come from.
Define a clear, differentiated brand position and set the creative standard for every campaign, launch and channel, holding internal teams and agencies to it.
Build and grow an agentic marketing team spanning creative, digital, and product and channel marketing for B2C and Pro/B2B, using AI agents for analytics, reporting, content and campaign operations; manage agency partners across media, creative, PR and web.
Brand Growth & Innovation
Build and scale the Yale and August brands in new and innovative ways, going beyond category-standard marketing to earn attention, advocacy and loyalty, and making home security feel personal rather than transactional.
Launch and grow creator, influencer, community and customer-advocacy programs and turn them into a repeatable engine for acquisition and word of mouth.
Build brand partnerships and ecosystem co-marketing with smart home platforms, builders, property managers, insurers and lifestyle brands that open new customer segments and routes to market.
Identify and pilot emerging growth channels and formats (such as social commerce, short-form video, in-store experiences and AI-driven discovery) against clear hypotheses; scale what wins and stop what does not.
Customer Insight & Product Marketing
Own quantitative customer and market insight (behavioral data, surveys, market share and channel data) that focuses Design's qualitative research, and use the combined findings with Product Management to drive product and marketing decisions and measure their results.
Partner with Product Management on the roadmap, portfolio, pricing and category view, representing customer needs, whitespace and competitive differentiation.
Lead launch marketing from concept through post-launch, designing launches that create buzz and drive trial, with value propositions for each audience, from homeowners to installers, dealers, integrators and property managers, and success metrics set before launch.
Measurement & Commercial Performance
Own the marketing OKRs and an integrated scorecard connecting investment to revenue, share, sell-through, ROAS, CAC, conversion and brand metrics; report results to business leadership and hold the team and agencies accountable to them.
Own working media across search, social, retail media, programmatic and CTV, allocating spend based on measured return.
Run a test-and-learn discipline across channels, reserving budget for bold experiments, spotting underperformance early and shifting strategy and spend to what works.
Omnichannel, Ecomm & Retail
Own the omnichannel experience so Yale and August show up consistently across D2C, Amazon, retailer sites, stores and Pro channels.
Drive discovery and conversion through search (SEO, AEO, GEO), ratings and reviews, enhanced content and accurate product data.
Partner with retail, ecomm and Pro sales teams on channel plans, co-op, sales enablement, point-of-purchase and partner activation programs.
Lifecycle & Content
Turn Design's customer journey plans into lifecycle programs that drive measurable device activation and engagement, and turn customers into loyal advocates through onboarding, referral and loyalty programs.
Set content priorities and an AI-first production model so every channel gets the right content on time.

The NPD Senior Mechanical Design Engineer plays a key role in driving mechanical design execution across one or more new product development programs, with responsibility for the design and development of cordless and pneumatic power fastening tools primarily used in wood and concrete applications. This position emphasizes deep hands-on technical contribution and problem-solving skills while progressively taking ownership of project-level decision-making, design direction, and coordination across functions. Leads project-level mechanical design execution, leveraging strong technical judgment and project planning skills to define scope, coordinate task-level resources, and deliver committed program objectives on time and within established constraints.

Performs and drives critical design analyses such as DFMEA, Design of Experiments, Tolerance Stack-ups, and serviceability assessments to proactively identify risks and ensure alignment with product requirements and specifications.
Takes responsibility for the integrated mechanical design of electro-mechanical devices and subsystems used in power fastening systems, ensuring proper layout, interface definition, design integration, validation, and documentation.
Coordinates prototype builds and validation activities, overseeing the production of prototypes and test units and supporting transition to manufacturing while ensuring quality standards, delivery schedules, and cost targets are met.

Executes complex assignments with increasing autonomy, demonstrating initiative, sound engineering judgment, and ownership while progressively expanding influence and leadership within the project team.
Partners closely with cross-functional teams including marketing, purchasing, manufacturing, quality, and suppliers to define project scope, assess cost targets, and ensure manufacturing feasibility throughout development.
Qualifications

8+ years of relevant product mechanical - design, including 2+ years in product development
Demonstrated experience working within structured, stage‑based product development frameworks,

Strong understanding of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools.
Demonstrated design capability, problem solving skills and ability to understand and trouble shoot electro-mechanical equipment.
Demonstrated experience of structured problem‑solving and continuous improvement methodologies, including A3’s Problem Solving, 8D, Fishbone (Ishikawa), cause‑and‑effect diagrams & 5 Why’s.
Experience in Leading design reviews, DFMEA, PFMEA, DVP&R, and root cause analysis sessions.
Strong understanding of modeling and simulation tools capabilities (FEA, CFD)
Advanced understanding of statistical tools such as FRD, DOE, COV, SPC, Pareto Analysis, etc.
Strong understanding of materials, manufacturing processes, and mechanical analysis including, plastic injection, stamping, aluminum, casting, machining, etc.
Experience in cross-functional collaboration to industrialize new products.
Experience with prototyping, testing, and production tooling.

The Product Commercialization Engineer will get to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, leading the scale-up and commercialization of adhesive, coating, and polymer technologies from laboratory development to full-scale manufacturing. This hands-on role partners with R&D, Operations, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Procurement, and Supply Chain to solve scale-up challenges and ensure products are manufactured safely, reliably, and cost-effectively across epoxy, acrylic/methacrylate, polyurethane, and hybrid polymer systems. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of driving innovation and growth for a division within a market-leading, Fortune 200 organization!
ITW BUSINESS MODEL & CULTURE
We have an environment shaped by our decentralized, entrepreneurial culture that brings our exciting ideas to life.  Our people thrive in our “flexibility within the framework” approach.
We are committed to providing you with growth and development opportunities that maximize your unique potential.

Be a part of One ITW/One Team, where everyone’s contribution matters in our quest to achieve our full potential.

Are an entrepreneurial self-starter. You take initiative and ownership of your surroundings and constantly seek to find ways to improve.
Thrive in a fast-paced environment that keeps you on your toes – you love a good challenge, meeting aggressive deadlines, and can stay calm under pressure.

Product Commercialization & Scale-Up
Lead commercialization and scale-up of new adhesive, coating, and polymer products from lab to full-scale manufacturing.
Develop robust, reproducible, and scalable manufacturing processes using chemical engineering principles and process science.
Identify and mitigate scale-up risks related to mixing, reaction control, heat transfer, equipment capability, and process variability.
Define operating windows and critical process parameters to ensure quality, consistency, and manufacturability.
Manufacturing & Process Improvement
Serve as a technical expert in polymer chemistry, process control, mixing, manufacturability, and raw material interactions.
Drive process improvements that enhance safety, quality, throughput, cost efficiency, and waste reduction while maintaining product performance.
Lead manufacturing troubleshooting, root-cause investigations, and resolution of batch variability and scale-dependent performance issues.
Apply DOE, statistical analysis, and structured problem-solving tools to optimize processes and resolve manufacturing challenges.

Lead evaluation, validation, and implementation of raw material, process, equipment, and manufacturing site changes, including alternative and second-source materials.
Identify, evaluate, and implement new manufacturing technologies, process controls, equipment, and analytical tools that support commercialization and operational excellence.
Support equipment qualification, process commissioning, manufacturing start-ups, and production readiness activities.
Safety, Quality & Leadership
Provide technical leadership across R&D, Operations, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, suppliers, and external partners to deliver safe, compliant, cost-effective, and successful product commercialization.
Promote, support, and adhere to all safety, environmental and quality related policies and procedures .

Minimum 5 years of experience in product/process scale-up and commercialization within a chemical manufacturing environment, including transfer from laboratory through pilot to commercial production.
Demonstrated experience bridging R&D/product development and manufacturing operations, including technology transfer and support of production scale-up between sites. Demonstrated track record of successfully commercializing new products at industrial production scale.
Strong knowledge of chemical engineering fundamentals, including mixing, heat transfer, mass transfer, reaction engineering, process control, and industrial manufacturing equipment/processes.
Proven ability to troubleshoot manufacturing and product-quality issues using structured problem-solving methods, including DOE, statistical analysis, process data analysis, and root-cause investigation; proficiency with tools such as JMP or Minitab preferred.
Demonstrated experience qualifying raw materials and alternate sources in incumbent commercial products.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical, operational, and manufacturing teams.
Experience preferred in the adhesives, coatings, sealants, specialty polymers, or formulated chemical products industries, primarily with epoxy, polyurethane, acrylic/methacrylate, and/or hybrid polymer chemistries.

description:
Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
Service/Repair Technician 1 is entry level in the service technician occupation requiring fundamental knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical aptitude with some troubleshooting experience. Responsible for providing on-site support to Hobart Service customers that includes but is not limited to: installation and/ or service of commercial food equipment. Routine work schedule including on-call, after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-site repair support.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
These are the most significant job duties performed. The size, scope and complexity of assigned duties and responsibilities are dependent on the level and experience of the incumbent. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each assigned essential duty satisfactorily. Other responsibilities or special projects not specifically listed below may also be assigned.
Installs basic mechanical commercial food equipment and assists in more advanced installs as needed.
Maintain, diagnose, and repair basic mechanical commercial food equipment for customers on contract and/or on time and material (i.e., T&M) basis.
Completes and documents preventative maintenance on basic mechanical commercial food equipment.
Implements and supports standard operating procedures outlined in Hobart Service safety manuals and programs.
Supports branch and organization financial objectives by providing a quality customer experience.
Maintains current organization, industry, and equipment knowledge.
Responsible for assigned company assets including vehicle, tools, and inventory.
Follows the company's safe driving and other applicable policies.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Required Education and Work Experience
High school diploma or GED and,
0-2 years of electrical/mechanical experience
Desired Education/Experience
Associates Degree or Vocational Certificate is preferred.
Mechanical or electrical experience is preferred.
Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing commercial cooking and/or refrigeration equipment is preferred.
Certificates and Licenses
Position/Location dependent.
Job Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
Mechanical Aptitude – demonstrates mechanical aptitude to operate and troubleshoot equipment. Skilled in use of various tools and equipment (e.g. basic hand tools, reading and following service manuals, gauges, meters, etc.)
Customer Service - highly professional demeanor with excellent telephone skills and etiquette. Utilizes various interpersonal styles and communication methods to positively assist and influence customers.
Problem Solving - fundamental role in finding ways to address all types of problems by having a good approach to a problem without being ineffective, favoring or causing painful consequences.
Safety at Work - learns to keep the organization safe from different risks by developing a high sense of alertness that detects danger from afar and stops it before it causes risk, danger or injury to themselves, or others.

Technical and Analytical Skills
Ability to read and interpret standard service manuals, mechanical diagrams, sustains understanding of parts stocking and identification methods, practices, and procedures.

Ensure they are following workflow processes (e.g., Inspection accuracy)

Completes tasks on time.

Ability to approach job responsibilities with an emphasis on safety, efficiency, and quality.

Demonstrates a comprehensive knowledge of company products and services.
Completes required safety training.

Prioritizes regular workload, special tasks and concurrent projects, allocating time and resources to ensure that work is completed accurately and efficiently within established time frame.
Demonstrated ability to communicate orally with individuals from within and outside the organization.

Thrives in multi-tasking environment and can adjust priorities quickly.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Physical Demands

Occasional roof access may be necessary through extension ladders or fixed ladders greater than 20 feet
Extensive walking 3-5 miles / day

Move in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments including tight and confined spaces

title: Sr Buyer - Precision Welding Solutions Divison
description:
Job Description:
The Senior Buyer is a key supply chain leader responsible for driving procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, and continuous improvement initiatives within the Precision Welding Solutions Division. In this role you will partner closely with the Materials Manager, suppliers, engineering and cross-functional teams to ensure excellence in cost, quality and delivery.
You will provide leadership, develop talent and drive results across the Precision Welding Solutions Division.  The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong negotiation and relationship building skills and can drive change through collaboration and influence.
How You Will Make an Impact:
Supply Chain & Procurement
Manage procurement activities, including sourcing, purchasing, inventory planning, and material flow.
Lead supplier negotiations involving pricing, contracts, delivery performance, and service levels.
Evaluate, select, and develop suppliers in partnership with the Materials Manager and engineering team.
Build collaborative supplier relationships while identifying opportunities for supplier consolidation and risk reduction.
Conduct supplier visits, audits, and performance reviews.
Manage supplier corrective action processes and ensure timely resolution of quality or delivery issues.
Monitor and communicate Market Rate of Demand (MRD) changes to suppliers
Cost & Inventory Management
Drive cost reduction, productivity, quality, delivery, and simplification initiatives.
Manage material price variance, inventory turns, and inventory optimization programs.
Track and document cost savings and cost avoidance projects.
Maintain inventory accuracy through cycle count oversight and inventory management practices.
Support inventory transition activities related to product launches, engineering changes, and product obsolescence.
Manage MOH and inactive inventory performance metrics.
Strategic Initiatives
Lead or support divisional materials and supply chain improvement projects.
Develop and implement materials strategies aligned with business objectives.
Actively participate in New Product Development (NPD) initiatives.
Partner daily with manufacturing, engineering, and other cross-functional teams to ensure material availability and operational continuity.
Champion and implement ITW business principles, including 80/20, Product Line Simplification, Market Rate of Demand (MRD), Empowerment, Trust, and Continuous Improvement.
