Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.

compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.

new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.

Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.

 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:

• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance

 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.

Normal office conditions.

Abhility to lift, maneuver, and troubleshoot fixture s and tools

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers (Systems Analysts) at Intuitive Surgical play a critical role in developing the safest, highest-quality robotic platforms for minimally invasive surgery through rigorous engineering analysis, innovative problem-solving, and robust technical execution.
Systems Analysts are central to the design, development, integration, and lifecycle support of next-generation products across the da Vinci Surgical System portfolio. They are responsible for developing, optimizing, and validating algorithms that govern robotic manipulator motion, force control, and system safety across surgical robots, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes.
The role requires broad systems-level expertise and close collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines, including mechanical, software, controls, user interface, electrical, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts provide early technical input into product architecture and design decisions, rapidly evaluate and validate new concepts, and proactively address complex challenges in system integration, functional safety, motion and force control, and manufacturing.
Their ownership extends throughout the product development lifecycle, from early feasibility and architecture through design verification, system integration, manufacturing readiness, and commercial release. The ultimate objective is to deliver innovative robotic technologies that meet the highest standards of safety, quality, performance, and reliability for surgeons and patients.
The Manager of a Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering (Systems Analysis) team establishes responsibilities within their team. They are responsible for defining and meeting project milestones. They advise senior management on the technical strategy for product and platform projects. They work closely with other algorithms & controls, software, hardware, manufacturing, and clinical engineering teams to enable cohesion of design inputs, design architecture, specifications, and verification. They are expected to hire, coach, and retain Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering talent within their group

Manage and support a team of Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers towards successful accomplishment of product implementation with best-in-class solutions and architectures
Hire, retain key talent required for the team to be successful.
Provide in-depth analysis and characterization of electromechanical architectures during the entire design life cycle.
Facilitate mechanical, electrical, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete robotic systems, manipulators, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes

The Upstream Reimbursement Strategist is the architect of the organization’s long-range reimbursement and market access strategy across the U.S. product portfolio. This person is responsible for generating all strategies for all upstream programs and dovetailing those strategies with global market access for ex-U.S. projects. This role is the closest link to the clinical development team and serves as the primary strategic interface with HEOR, regulatory affairs, and health policy stakeholders.
Responsible for evidence generation strategy, CPT/HCPCS code pathway design, CMS payment policy analysis, and the global coordination of evidence that feeds both upstream regulatory submissions and downstream field execution tools. This person shapes the narrative for why a product deserves reimbursement and builds the data package to support it.
Core Responsibilities
CPT/HCPCS Code Strategy: Lead the strategy for new code applications, Category III code conversions, and descriptor modifications. Manage engagement with AMA CPT Editorial Panel, RUC, and HCPCS workgroups.
CMS Payment Policy Analysis: Conduct ongoing analysis of OPPS, PFS, and ASC payment policy. Prepare and submit CMS comment letters during rulemaking cycles. Monitor NT-APC, pass-through, and device payment category developments.
Global Evidence Coordination: Serve as the connective tissue between U.S. evidence needs and global HEOR and OUS markets. Dovetail U.S. upstream strategies with global market access to ensure alignment on ex-U.S. projects. Ensure evidence generation is sequenced to serve both U.S. regulatory/payer needs and ex-U.S. HTA submissions, coordinating timing and deliverables across jurisdictions.
Coverage & Reimbursement Strategy: Generate and own the reimbursement strategy for all upstream programs across the full product portfolio. Develop and maintain the strategic reimbursement roadmap from early pipeline through commercialization, including target product profiles (TPPs) and core value dossiers (CVDs) for pipeline assets. Identify coverage gaps, analyze competitive reimbursement positioning, recommend pathway strategies, and ensure strategic continuity as products progress through development milestones.
U.S. Value Plan Implementation Support: Play a supporting role to HEOR in ensuring the U.S. Market Access team has secured the database resources required to execute strategy and implement the recommendations set out in the U.S. Value Plan.
Competitive Intelligence: Monitor competitor reimbursement strategies, code applications, pass-through approvals, and coverage determinations. Translate competitive intelligence into actionable strategic recommendations.

Market Access Research: Lead market access research to support value messaging, including claims analyses and — where needed — coordination of payer interviews, provider interviews, and other primary research.
Shared Midstream Responsibility: Contribute to code acquisition execution, pre-launch payer engagement planning, and payment policy implementation activities in partnership with the Mid/Downstream Tactician.

Health policy degree or similar
3-8+ years of progressive experience in medical device market access, health economics, reimbursement strategy, or related field (for manager level, 3+)
Deep working knowledge of CMS OPPS/PFS/ASC payment systems, APC mechanics, and facility payment methodology
Experience with CPT, , AMA Editorial Panel processes, and HCPCS coding pathways
Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting claims data, cost reports, and CMS rulemaking documents
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex policy into strategic recommendations
Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, regulatory, HEOR, and commercial teams

Advanced degree (MPH, MBA, or equivalent; PhD or PharmD also welcome)

Creating and leading data driven cross-functional engineering team meetings to address manufacturing issues.

Minimum 5 years experience as design or manufacturing engineer supporting product with significant electromechanical content.
Sense of curiosity and a willingness to always dig deeper.
Ability to read electronic and mechanical schematics, assembly, and fabrication drawings.  Execute testing and data collection using Linux, Matlab, and other software toolsets.
Strong skills in problem solving and using Minitab/JMP, Python, SQL, Tableau and/or other SW tools for data analysis to identify root cause and drive corrective actions.

BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering/Science, or Mechanical Engineering.
MS degree in Engineering preferred.

Ability to sit and stand for long periods of time
Ability to lift, and carry parts weighing up to 40 lbs
Ability to maneuver into spaces around robotic system

“Self-starter” attitude and comfort in a hands-on environment, where he/she can demonstrate an ability to work with other engineers to influence product and manufacturing design to improve reliability.
Experience in an ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or medical device manufacturing environment
Experience and proficiency in ERP, CRM, PLM software including SAP and Agile.
Experience with use of EE lab equipment including Oscilloscopes, Spectrum Analyzers, Power supplies, and Multimeters

Services Technical Publications provides the foundation for every procedure performed on Intuitive's advanced medical devices by the global Field Service team. Our content is authored in DITA and delivered through guided workflows, which progressively discloses content for field service technicians install, maintain, and repair Intuitive systems.
In this role, you will combine expert editing skills with strategic thinking to develop and implement a comprehensive quality metrics program. You will work directly with technical writers, product teams, and stakeholders to ensure that hardware and software documentation meets our highest standards for clarity, accuracy, consistency, and usability within guided, step-by-step workflows.
As an individual contributor with significant influence and authority, your success will be measured by your ability to drive quality improvements and positive outcomes through collaboration, coaching, and strategic program development—not through direct management, but through leadership and expertise.
Essential Job Duties
Edit hardware and software technical documentation for clarity, accuracy, consistency, voice, tone, and usability. Champion minimalist, task-based writing principles to ensure content serves the immediate needs of field service technicians. Work directly with authors and SMEs to improve content quality across the publication lifecycle.
Make edits directly in IXIA, our component content management system, collaborating with technical writers and subject matter experts through the review workflow to implement changes efficiently. Comfort navigating the system and driving content improvements end-to-end.
Develop and own a quality metrics program that establishes baselines, identifies improvement opportunities, and measures impact. Use data-driven insights to guide editorial strategy and demonstrate ROI of editing services.
Design and implement best practices for technical content quality. Create scalable processes, guidelines, and checklists that enable teams to self-serve and maintain consistency without bottlenecking editorial review.
Lead training and coaching initiatives. Educate writers on minimalism, task-based authoring, topic-based writing principles, style, and grammar standards. Establish regular office hours, workshops, or feedback sessions to build writer capability and confidence.
Configure and integrate content quality tools (Acrolinx, Congree, Grammarly, or similar) into the publication workflow. Recommend technology solutions that enhance quality without creating friction for authors.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including product, UX, localization, and publishing—to align on quality standards and resolve editorial challenges.
Required Skills and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
7+ years of professional editing experience in technical communications, with demonstrated expertise editing DITA-authored content for both hardware and software products.
Deep expertise in minimalist and task-based, topic-based authoring approaches. Demonstrated ability to coach authors on these principles and evaluate content for adherence to minimalist standards.
Proficiency with IXIA or similar component content management systems (CCMS). Ability to navigate the system, make edits directly, and move content through review workflows independently.
Experience developing or implementing editorial guidelines, style guides, or content quality standards. Comfort with creating scalable, repeatable processes.
Proficiency with quality assurance tools such as Acrolinx, Congree, Grammarly, or equivalent. Ability to evaluate tools and troubleshoot configuration issues.
Proven ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both in written and spoken formats. Skill in explaining complex editorial feedback in a way that educates rather than demoralizes.
Experience working with metrics, data collection, or quality measurement. Comfort with analyzing trends and using data to support recommendations.
Ability to influence and drive outcomes without direct authority. Success collaborating with subject matter experts, product teams, and writers who may not report to you.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with medical device, surgical instrument, or other regulated/high-stakes technical documentation.
Familiarity with content management systems, publishing workflows, or localization processes.
Experience training or coaching other writers or editors.
Understanding of how DITA-authored content serves guided workflows with progressive disclosure, and how editing decisions impact both user experience and compliance.

Primary Function of Position:
As a Vision Software Staff Engineer, you will act as the technical lead for the software and embedded architecture definition of the real-time, high-definition video processing, imaging, and intra-body illumination systems at the heart of a new generation surgical robotic platform.
You will drive the deep integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, bringing sound engineering judgment to the trade-offs between hardware, software, and algorithms, and procedure-specific product requirements.
Critical to the success of this role is experience diagnosing and debugging complex vision systems end-to-end – from sensor and optics through the video pipeline to software – driving root cause investigations and collaborating with hardware and algorithms teams to resolve difficult, multi-disciplinary issues. Familiarity with working in a regulated industry and with design controls for medical devices is a plus.
The successful candidate must excel at evaluating design trade-offs through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration, translating rough requirements into robust, well-reasoned embedded software architectures.
A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required, as is the ability to make the work fun and interesting. Supporting you will be a development and management team that knows and cares about what you are doing and wants you to succeed.
Essential Job Duties
Lead the definition of hardware, software, and algorithms architecture for the real-time video processing engine, image sensors, and intra-body illumination systems of a new generation surgical robotic platform, from concept through implementation.
Drive the integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, ensuring robust interfaces between hardware, FPGA/ISP, and software components.
Evaluate multiple design trade-offs for the embedded vision software architecture through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration.
Lead bring-up and integration of new, high-performance cameras and image sensors, and the integration and evaluation of advanced camera pipeline video processing algorithms.
Diagnose and debug vision system issues end-to-end – sensor, optics, video pipeline, and software – leading root cause investigations in close collaboration with hardware, algorithms, and systems engineering teams.
Drive development and enhancement of the color and power control functions for intra-operative illumination.
Lead formal risk analyses for vision and illumination subsystems; identify additional hardware requirements and develop software mitigations to minimize potential failures.
Design and develop offline simulation environments and hardware/software diagnostic tools that accelerate development, debug, and test.
Perform and guide detailed design, development, documentation, and verification of embedded vision software and supervisory state machines, in compliance with regulatory requirements and Intuitive's internal guidelines.
Contribute broadly across the video and vision software stack, including extension of current processing frameworks to new hardware platforms.
Apply high-level and specialized imaging/vision expertise to deliver innovations and problem-solving approaches that can be leveraged across multiple products.
Mentor and guide engineers across the vision team.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a similar technical field.
A minimum of 12 years of experience developing and supporting embedded systems, with significant focus on video, imaging, or vision systems (or 8 years with a Master's degree, or 5 years with a PhD).
Required Skills and Experience
Fluent in designing and developing mission-critical, cross-platform code in C/C++ for embedded, real-time, Linux-based systems, including application-level and driver-level development for multi-core and multi-processor architectures.
Deep familiarity with integrating cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex embedded architectures, including hardware, software, and algorithm interfaces.
Demonstrated ability to debug and diagnose complex vision system issues through root cause investigation and close cross-functional collaboration with hardware and algorithms teams.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate design trade-offs for embedded software architectures through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration.
Direct experience with imaging devices – e.g., cameras, light sensors, video/graphics hardware – including sensor and camera bring-up, configuration, and integration.
Fluent with image-processing concepts, camera pipeline video processing algorithms, and video processing frameworks.
Working knowledge of Python or other scripting languages for diagnostics, automation, and test.
Demonstrated experience and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle, including design, documentation, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Knowledge of image-processing, CUDA, ML, and/or FPGA integration (e.g., Vivado and other FPGA development tools).
Familiarity with communication protocols such as TCP/IP, CAN, and serialization protocols.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for mission-critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.
Leadership of medical technology projects from inception through field validation to launch; strong understanding of the medical product ecosystem.
Familiarity with rapid development and rapid prototyping tools.
Demonstrated capacity to relate to and mentor all levels of employees.

Experience troubleshooting complex software and integrated system-level issues
Experience developing internal engineering or automation tools
Experience with Python
Ability to analyze logs, trace failures, and perform root cause analysis
Experience with embedded systems, firmware, or hardware validation environments

Experience supporting robotics, medical device, embedded, or complex hardware/software integrated systems

Primary Function of Position:
A Systems Analyst is responsible for the detailed design and implementation of robotic control algorithms and safety systems for new surgical robots and instruments. This includes integrating and evaluating fully functional prototypes and conducting formal product testing.
Systems Analysts also provide analytical support to other engineering groups in designing mechanisms, software architecture, and selecting key components, utilizing both physical and algorithmic insights to ensure safe, reliable, and precise motion control performance and high-level behaviors in response to user inputs.
Quick learning and a keen understanding of both user and engineering perspectives are essential,
As part of the Future Forward engineering team, you will design, implement, and integrate complex functionalities into complete surgical robot solutions, overseeing them through human use and product release. You will be part of a high-energy, focused team, with a strong sense of shared responsibility and reward.
Essential Job Duties:
Contribute to the design of new robot manipulators and new robotic instruments through analysis and characterization of prototypes.
Refine and evolve system performance as it matures to a full product stage.
Facilitate mechanical, hardware, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete systems, manipulators, and vision.
Provide critical analysis of robot servo control and design fault-detection algorithms.
Provide analytical assistance for other engineering issues.
Document and communicate intellectual property.
Improve group workflow through tool building and robust cross-functional interactions.
Required Education and Training:
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering, or similar technical field, with 3 years of experience in control systems, servo control, or robotics.
Alternatively, a Ph.D. degree in one of the technical fields above, with no experience.

Experience implementing, tuning, and debugging modern servo control systems.
Expert knowledge of robot modeling and system identification techniques.
Experience in designing and developing real-time control algorithms in C or C++, with the ability to assess numerical accuracy and computational complexity.
Working knowledge of Python or MATLAB/Simulink for control system simulation, analysis, and testing.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of an organization.
Excitement to learn, solve tough technical problems, and to help improve patients' lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience:
Expert in one or more advanced robotic control concepts such as impedance control or the control of flexible manipulators.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for safety-critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.
Fluent working with software version control systems such as Git.
Working knowledge of embedded Linux or QNX at multiple levels including application, board bring-up, device drivers and distribution configuration.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.

description:
Hourly manufacturing position
Job Description
The Electro-Mechanical Technician is responsible for performing preventative, predictive, and routine maintenance on production and facility equipment. This role troubleshoots and repairs electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and controls-related equipment to help maximize equipment reliability, efficiency, and uptime.

Minimum of 2 years of industrial maintenance experience involving electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, or controls-related equipment.
Experience troubleshooting and repairing production or manufacturing equipment.
Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills.
Ability to safely diagnose equipment problems and determine appropriate corrective actions.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Strong communication and teamwork skills.

3-phase 480V electrical systems
PLC and ladder logic troubleshooting
Allen-Bradley ControlLogix
RSLogix 5000
Motors, drives, sensors, and control panels
DCS/PLC control systems

Preventative and predictive maintenance programs
SAP or another CMMS

What’s on the menu?
We are looking for a Staff Architect – ERP Capabilities to join the Kraft Heinz TECH Architecture Team and support the evolution of Kraft Heinz's global ERP landscape.
In this role, you will provide SAP platform and architecture expertise across ERP capabilities, partnering with business teams, functional IT leaders, architects, and technology teams to guide solution decisions and support business transformation.
The role combines architecture leadership with hands-on solution design guidance. You will contribute to major ERP initiatives such as SAP S/4HANA, provide architectural input for business demands and solution designs, participate in architecture governance activities, and help advance ERP architecture practices across the organization.
The ideal candidate is a strong SAP professional with an architecture mindset, capable of understanding the broader SAP ecosystem, evaluating solution options, and translating architecture principles into practical solutions that deliver business value.
Key Ingredients:
ERP Architecture & SAP Platform
Provide architecture leadership for assigned ERP domains, covering SAP S/4HANA, ECC and the broader SAP ecosystem (BTP, SAP AI/Joule, SAP Fiori, MDG, SAP Integration Suite, OpenText, SAP DRC and others), translating business requirements into scalable and maintainable solutions.
Collaborate with ERP functional teams, solution architects and IT leaders to implement architecture principles, standards and patterns, promoting simplification and reducing unnecessary complexity.
S/4HANA Transformation
Support architecture activities within SAP S/4HANA transformation programs and strategic ERP initiatives, contributing to target-state designs and architecture decisions across functional and technical teams.
Advocate for SAP standard processes, Fit-to-Standard, Clean Core and extensibility principles, helping teams evaluate alternatives and minimize customizations where appropriate
Integration & Technical Architecture
Drive architecture decisions for SAP and non-SAP integration, including APIs, events, middleware and SAP Integration Suite, working with development and integration teams to deliver scalable and maintainable solutions.
Lead the review of technical options and solution designs, challenging assumptions, identifying dependencies, risks and trade-offs, and driving teams toward pragmatic technology decisions.
Architecture & Solution Guidance
Lead ERP architecture assessment within the Architecture Review Board (ARB), challenging new demands, projects and solution designs and driving clear architecture recommendations and decisions.
Guide and challenge functional and solution teams throughout the solution lifecycle, ensuring designs align with ERP architecture principles, standards, patterns and business outcomes.
Stakeholder & Architecture Capability
Build strong partnerships with ERP functional leaders, solution architects, Enterprise Architecture and technology teams, and represent ERP Architecture in relevant technology evaluations, RFPs and solution selections.
Drive selected architecture chapter initiatives and ways of working, developing reusable patterns and standards, sharing knowledge and mentoring architects and functional teams to strengthen architecture capability across Kraft Heinz TECH.
Recipe for Success: Apply if this sounds like you!
Essential Qualifications
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
5-8 years of experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, or senior technical design roles supporting complex enterprise platforms.
Strong hands-on experience with SAP ecosystems, including one or more of the following: SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, SAP BTP, SAP Integration Suite, SAP PI/PO, SAP Fiori, SAP MDG, SAP BW/4HANA, or related SAP backend technologies.
Strong understanding of backend enterprise capabilities, including integrations, APIs, middleware, event-driven architecture, master data, batch and real-time processing, and enterprise security considerations.
Experience guiding architecture across complex ERP landscapes that include SAP and non-SAP platforms.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and drive architecture decisions without direct authority.
Strong understanding of system scalability, resilience, security, supportability, and lifecycle management in enterprise backend environments.
Experience contributing to architecture standards, review processes, roadmaps, and reusable design patterns.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical recommendations to both technical teams and senior non-technical stakeholders.
Nice to have
Exposure to SAP RISE/Cloud ERP architectures, FIORI and modern SAP development approaches.
SAP, TOGAF or other relevant architecture certifications.

title: Retail Sales Manager - Bentonville (AR)
description:
Job Description:
Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that RSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions, enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, RSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.
Job Specifications/Qualifications
This role is an individual contributor.
This role interfaces with customers at store level
This role has a reasonable impact on sales organizations and a reasonable impact on the company.
Education & Professional Qualification:
Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge/Experience
Minimum Qualifications :
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

title: Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives – Better For You
description:
Job Description:
Who are we?
Accelerator, a global Division of Mars Snacking, is on the front line of unlocking growth across high-potential categories and brands to fuel what’s next for Snacking. It’s home to both emerging and enduring brands, including KIND, TRÜ FRÜ, NATURE’S BAKERY, RXBAR, EGGO, POP-TARTS and RICE KRISPIE TREATS. Combining the scale of Mars with the agility of a start-up, our Division has the ambition to accelerate the future of snacking by delivering products consumers love today, discovering category-shaping innovations for tomorrow and developing entrepreneurial teams whose impact will last for generations.
We’re looking for passionate talent who dare to dream big, agile collaborators who talk straight and decide fast, and driven performers with a growth mindset. We’re proudly part of Mars, while also building something boldly different. If this inspires and energizes you, you’ve found the right place where you can do cool things with fun people for one of the biggest snacking companies in the world!
What will you do?
Reporting to the General Manager, Better-For-You (BFY), the Sr. Director, Strategic Initiatives serves as a key architect of the BFY business strategy and operating agenda. The Better-For-You portfolio includes KIND, RX, Pure Organic, Nutri-Grain, Special K Bars, and Kashi Bars across North America (US and Canada), spanning founder-led insurgency brands through scaled growth platforms. This role partners across Commercial, Supply, Finance, R&D, Strategy, and Enterprise functions to identify, prioritize, and deliver the initiatives that create sustainable growth and improve overall business performance.
As a member of the Better For You Leadership Team, this leader drives Business Unit and enterprise-wide strategic priorities, coordinating complex cross-functional initiatives, accelerating decision-making, and ensuring the organization remains focused on the highest-value opportunities of today and the future. Success requires a unique combination of strategic thinking, business acumen, influence, organizational leadership, and execution excellence.
What would be your key responsibilities?
Shape and Drive the Better For You Growth Agenda
Partner with the General Manager and Leadership Team to develop and refine the BFY portfolio's multi-year growth strategy.
Identify strategic choices and steppingstones within brands, across portfolio and innovation, and among channels / customers,
Translate strategy into actionable business priorities, roadmaps, investment recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
Drive near term performance while maintaining an eye toward future-back trends / disruptions (consumer, regulatory, ecosystem) that will impact Snacking.
Lead Enterprise Strategic Initiatives
Own a portfolio of high-priority business initiatives that require cross-functional leadership and enterprise coordination.
Serve as the leadership team's quarterback for transformational programs, business integrations, capability builds, and operating model improvements.
Drive disciplined execution, governance, risk management, and issue resolution across strategic initiatives.
Ensure critical projects remain on schedule, deliver expected outcomes, and generate measurable business impact.
Partner Across the Business to Improve Performance
Collaborate closely with Brand, Sales, Customer, Supply Chain, Finance, R&D, and Strategy to deliver the full potential of the business and supporting value creation algorithm (growth, P&L shape, and earnings position).
Diagnose business challenges and opportunities through data-driven analysis and prepare fact-based recommendations.
Facilitate dynamic resource allocation and investment decisions across competing business priorities.
Support annual planning, long-range planning, and portfolio reviews.
Drive Leadership Team Effectiveness
Partner with the General Manager to establish leadership team priorities, meeting effectiveness, decision-making processes, and execution rhythms.
Ensure alignment across the leadership team on strategic priorities, actions, accountabilities, and performance outcomes.
Facilitate cross-functional problem-solving and accelerate resolution of complex organizational issues.
Improve organizational focus by simplifying priorities and eliminating low-value activities.
Build Organizational Capabilities for Long-Term Success
Identify capability gaps that could constrain future growth and develop plans to address them.
Lead efforts to strengthen organizational effectiveness, ways of working, and cross-functional collaboration.
Support development of the BFY culture, employee engagement strategy, and leadership effectiveness initiatives.
Champion a culture of accountability, learning, agility, and continuous improvement.
Serve as a Strategic Advisor to the General Manager
Act as a trusted thought partner to the General Manager on business performance, organizational health, strategic choices, and change management.
Lead special projects, board-level analyses, executive presentations, and business reviews.
Prepare recommendations and materials for senior leadership discussions and key enterprise forums.
Represent the BFY business in cross-segment and enterprise strategic initiatives when appropriate.
What are we looking for?
12+ years of progressive leadership experience in Strategy, General Management, Commercial Leadership, Business Transformation, Management Consulting, Finance, or related business functions.
Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced business degree preferred.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing business strategy within consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, retail, or adjacent industries.
Strong business and financial acumen with experience evaluating growth opportunities, investments, organizational effectiveness, and business performance.
Proven track record leading complex cross-functional initiatives and delivering measurable business results.
Exceptional executive communication, storytelling, and influence skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable recommendations.
Experience working directly with senior executives and leadership teams.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, ambiguous, and highly collaborative environments.
Track record of building alignment and driving change without direct authority.
Experience leading teams and developing talent preferred.

Opportunity to shape the future of Better For You snacking across some of Mars’ most recognized brands.
Ability to combine the scale and global capabilities of Mars with the speed and agility of an entrepreneurial business.
High-visibility leadership role with strong cross-functional exposure and opportunities for continued career growth within Mars.
Opportunity to lead innovation while strengthening and growing the core Better For You portfolio.

Leads the planning and execution on opportunities with resources and partners to cross-sell, up-sell, and co-sell; identifies, leverages, coordinates partners and resources across solution areas, and supports on-boarding new partners; validates partner solution relevance for customers; provides input and feedback to One Commercial Partner (OCP) on developing partner strategies and consumption plans, and connects the partner ecosystems to scale business results.

title: Critical Environment Technician Manager
description:
Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Data Center Critical Environment Technician Manager.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I CE Technician Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Provides assignment and completion oversight of team members for mandatory, technical, and procedural training material. Assigns and oversees procedure development and reporting to team members. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Guides, oversees, and performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines and supports team members with subject matter expertise. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Provides and/or assigns team members to provide necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site for all procedure levels of risk (LOR). May take part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Engages to address and resolve circumstances when supplier/vendor work has been stopped to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates and/or assigns team members to coordinate across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. Reviews and approves vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Leads and provides guidance on coordinating activities and establishing associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. description:

The Growth team helps people and businesses discover, adopt, and get lasting value from ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. We partner with Brand Marketing, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and Creative to connect marketing investment with customer and business outcomes. Our brand data infrastructure brings together media, audience, creative, and research data so teams can plan, measure, and improve brand investment across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Brand Data Infrastructure Lead to own the data foundations that make brand marketing measurable and scalable. You will define how brand media, campaign, creative, audience, and research data are organized, connected, validated, and made available for decisions. This hands-on role combines brand and media expertise with practical data fluency, turning fragmented platform and partner outputs into dependable datasets and repeatable workflows.

This role sits within Growth Marketing and works closely with Brand Marketing, Media Operations, Growth Platform’s solutions engineering team, Data Engineering, and Data Science. You own Brand’s data roadmap, business definitions, source requirements, data-quality acceptance, and adoption. Engineering partners own production architecture, connector and pipeline implementation, instrumentation, and technical incident resolution. Data Science owns statistical methodology and model development.

Your first priority is to establish consistent campaign and creative taxonomies, dependable media and measurement feeds, clear data-sharing arrangements, and trusted reporting inputs. Build a foundation that supports TV/CTV, online video, social, audio, out-of-home, and other brand channels, with the coverage and history needed for brand tracking, lift studies, incrementally, and marketing mix modeling.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the Brand data infrastructure roadmap. Translate brand strategy, media plans, and measurement needs into prioritized data capabilities, source integrations, quality improvements, and reporting foundations. Balance business value, global coverage, delivery dependencies, cost, and sustained adoption.

 - Define shared data models and taxonomies. Establish consistent campaign, creative, channel, partner, audience, and market definitions, identifiers, reporting grains, and time conventions. Define the fields, granularity, history, coverage, refresh cadence, and reconciliation needed from platforms, agencies, publishers, and measurement vendors. Use source reports and delivered datasets to identify missing feeds, taxonomy gaps, duplication, and reporting discrepancies; assess business impact, coordinate resolution, and validate recovery with the accountable technical or vendor owner.

 - Build usable data products and handoffs. Partner with data and analytics teams on curated Brand datasets, reporting inputs, documentation, and self-service access. Maintain definitions, lineage, training, and support procedures so Brand leaders, regional teams, and measurement specialists can use the data consistently with less manual reconciliation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years of experience in marketing data, brand or media measurement, marketing technology, analytics operations, or related roles, including hands-on ownership of data capabilities that improved marketing decisions.

 - Understand data models, identifiers, taxonomy, data contracts, and quality checks, and how they support brand lift, incrementality, and marketing mix modeling. You can interpret source extracts and reporting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and work effectively with measurement specialists.

Familiarity with SQL-based analysis is valuable; deep coding expertise is not required.

description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As a Certification Assessment Specialist, you will design, build, test, launch, and maintain the hands-on assessments behind an OpenAI technical role-based certification. Your work will help candidates demonstrate what they can do in realistic scenarios and give reviewers reliable evidence to score their work.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role reporting to the Technical Certification Lead. You will turn competency models, assessment blueprints and scoring rubrics into working tasks, assessment environments and workflows that capture candidate evidence and produce results reviewers can verify. You will use scripting and automation and partner with engineering on software development and delivery integrations.

You will work with the certification, measurement, engineering and operations teams, as well as technical subject matter experts and external delivery providers. The Technical Certification Lead will coordinate alignment with learning content while keeping confidential assessment details separate from learning materials.

You will take assessments from prototype through pilot, launch, and ongoing maintenance across live and virtual delivery. As products and tools change, you will update tasks, environments, and scoring together so candidates are assessed against the intended skills.

Success means candidates have the opportunity to demonstrate the competencies required for the certification, and reviewers can consistently score that work using evidence they can trace back to the submission.

In this role, you will:

 - Translate assessment blueprints into realistic scenarios, candidate instructions, and hands-on tasks. Work with subject matter experts to check that the tasks reflect the job and elicit the appropriate evidence for each rubric.

 - Define assessment environment requirements and build or configure the environments candidates will use. Establish repeatable provisioning and reset workflows for accounts, tools, data, and permissions so candidates start from consistent conditions.

 - Build and maintain pipelines that capture candidate submissions and other scoring evidence, apply scoring rules, and route results for review. Make scores traceable to the underlying evidence and protect sensitive data under approved controls.

 - Build and test model-assisted scoring with qualified human reviewers using established validation criteria. Compare model scores with calibrated expert judgments, investigate disagreements, implement agreed rules for routing cases to human review, and rerun validation tests after material changes to the model, task, or rubric.

 - Test assessments end to end, from environment setup to evidence capture and scoring. Use dry runs and pilots to check instructions, timing, accessibility, and failure recovery; fix defects and verify the fixes before release. Test scoring against multiple valid approaches, partial and incorrect submissions, and failures in the assessment environment, so a platform issue isn’t mistaken for a candidate error.

 - Translate assessment needs into requirements for delivery integrations. Partner with engineering and delivery providers to test candidate access, submission and results handoffs and troubleshoot issues.

 - Prepare assessments for launch with platform and operations partners. Document setup, version dependencies, and troubleshooting so delivery teams can run assessments consistently and respond when something breaks.

 - Maintain versioned tasks, environments, scoring configurations, and test fixtures. Use candidate feedback and delivery and scoring data to identify issues, update or retire tasks, and check that changes preserve the intended skills and difficulty.

 - Investigate technical issues raised during delivery or candidate review. Reproduce defects where possible, document what was affected, and test fixes with the relevant delivery partners.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally designed and built performance-based, hands-on assessments, labs or simulations for technical roles, such as software developers or solution architects, and taken them through testing, launch and maintenance. Experience creating question-and-answer tests alone does not meet this requirement.

 - Have used scripting and automation to build and troubleshoot technical assessment environments. You can work with technical subject matter experts to translate realistic solutions into assessments; deep AI-engineering expertise or prior experience with a particular language or delivery platform is not required.

 - Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

 - Can use a blueprint and rubric to design realistic tasks and specify what evidence distinguishes competent performance from task completion.

 - Have built or maintained workflows that capture submissions, process evidence, and produce traceable scores or reviewer outputs.

 - Have implemented or validated model-assisted scoring or evaluation against expert human judgments, and can explain when a score should go to human review.

 - Have worked directly with external technical experts or delivery providers and can translate requirements into integrations you can test end to end.

 - Have used pilot results, candidate feedback, and scoring or delivery data to improve assessment quality.

 - Understand how to build for accessibility and protect candidate evidence and confidential assessment content.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to subject matter experts, measurement specialists, platform engineers, and operations teams.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

title: Data Scientist, Integrity
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

You’ll stay close enough to the engineering to help the team make difficult calls, whether that means running one more experiment on the bench or deciding that a change is ready to ship.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Modular Builds
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer for Data Center Modular Builds, you will own supplier manufacturing and integration quality for modular systems, including hot aisle containment (HAC), modular cooling units (MCUs), and electrical skids. Working with mechanical and electrical integrators and their suppliers, you will lead supplier qualification, support product and process development, and translate engineering requirements into manufacturing controls, inspections, and acceptance criteria.

You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds.

Key responsibilities

Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development

 - Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators.

 - Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids.

 - Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes.

 - Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results.

Site Escalations and Corrective Action

 - Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Verify root causes, track corrective and preventive actions to closure, and confirm their effectiveness.

 - Apply closed-loop learning (CLL) to incorporate field findings and lessons learned into supplier and integrator manufacturing controls and future builds, preventing recurrence.

Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring

 - Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers.

 - Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Coordinate deviation resolution and escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and manufacturing engineering.

 - Experience working with integrators and suppliers across multiple tiers to manage quality throughout the product lifecycle, from OFCI component manufacturing through integration and site issue resolution, and drive product and process improvements.

 - Ability to define CTQs and acceptance criteria, develop inspection and test checklists, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, conducting product and process audits, managing controlled documents and deviations, and using supplier scorecards to drive improvement.

 - Demonstrated experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing or field issues using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys, and driving continuous improvement through PDCA.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple equipment programs.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements, resolve issues, and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

title: Model Policy Manager, Emerging AI Misuse
description:
About the Team

The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards.

About the Role

As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

In this role, you will: 

 - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers.

 - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses.

 - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse.

 - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work.

 - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems.

 - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others.

 - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it.

 - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria.

 - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next.

 - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

 - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

 - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change.

 - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience building and shipping complex technical products, and a commitment to AI safety. You should be comfortable working through uncertainty, engaging deeply with research, and adapting direction as capabilities, evidence, and user needs evolve.
