title: Protection Scientist Engineer, Integrity
description:
About the Team

The Integrity team is responsible for the scaled systems that help identify and respond to bad actors and harm on OpenAI’s platforms. We protect users and the wider world by developing responses to complex harms and building the harm protections needed for new product and model launches. Integrity’s work spans not only across frontier harms like biological weapons and cybersecurity, but also high severity abuses such as child safety, nation-state misuse, and violence.

About the Role

Protection Scientists within Integrity design, orchestrate, and mature systems of defence against usage harms enabled by OpenAI's products. We are systems thinkers that combine deep harm domain expertise with breadth across investigation, data science, machine learning, policy and operations. Our distinctive strength is understanding how these disciplines fit together and translating between them to design and build effective systems of defence.

In San Francisco, we are hiring for protection work focused on sextortion, trafficking, national security (including nation-state misuse), and jailbreaks. Depending on your domain expertise, your work could include identifying AI-enabled coercion and exploitation, detecting misuse that supports trafficking, uncovering coordinated activity by state-linked actors, or investigating attempts to circumvent model safeguards. You will translate these evolving threats into detection systems and interventions that reduce harm.

Your core hands-on technical responsibility is harm detection. You will design, build, evaluate and maintain production detection systems, drawing on investigative expertise, data and shared engineering platforms. You will develop signals and classifiers that identify abusive behaviour and patterns across accounts and activity, and adapt them as adversaries change tactics.

You will also own the strategy and cross-functional delivery of protection work for a harm area or product launch. Working closely with investigators and other domain experts, you will ground the design in a deep understanding of how the harm occurs and translate that understanding into a system of defence. You will connect detection with policy, review, interventions, enforcement and measurement, continually calibrating the system against real cases and expert judgement as it scales.

You will identify what needs to be built or changed and make it happen. Success requires setting clear priorities, aligning partners, resolving dependencies and communicating evidence, decisions and trade-offs crisply. It also requires a willingness to jump in and work directly on whatever is blocking system effectiveness, using your breadth of skills.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and includes participation in an on-call rotation that may involve resolving urgent escalations outside normal working hours. Some investigations may involve sensitive content, including sexual, violent or otherwise disturbing material.

In this role, you will:

 - Define and drive protection strategy for a harm area or launch. Translate ambiguous risks into goals, priorities and roadmaps, and make trade-offs based on evidence, risk and available capacity.

 - Directly build and maintain harm detection. Develop production signals, classifiers and pipelines using SQL, Python, machine learning and language models, integrating with shared engineering platforms.

 - Lead cross-functional execution. Translate between specialist roles, establish shared understanding and ownership, resolve technical and organisational dependencies, and communicate recommendations and specific asks clearly.

 - Investigate exploitation and national security threats within your area of focus. Work with domain experts to understand actor behaviour, recognise patterns of coercion, exploitation or coordinated misuse, and turn case findings into detection criteria.

 - Connect detection to effective action. Partner with Policy and Operations to develop review and escalation protocols, distinguish abusive activity from legitimate use, and improve interventions as new cases reveal gaps.

 - Evaluate and improve the complete system of defence. Measure remaining harm, detection quality and intervention effectiveness and collaborate with Data Science on more sophisticated metrics. Use expert feedback and operational outcomes to guide improvements.

 - Protect product and model launches. Define data, detection and review requirements; establish monitoring; investigate gaps and critical escalations; and drive improvements informed by post-launch findings.

 - Scale effective approaches with language models, agents and reusable tools. Choose where automation and human judgement are needed, and build documentation and processes that improve reliability and help others extend the work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Think in systems. You have enough breadth across technical, analytical, investigative and operational disciplines to understand how they fit together, recognise gaps and translate between specialist perspectives.

 - Bring deep expertise in at least one of sextortion, trafficking, national security, jailbreaks or a closely related harm domain. Relevant backgrounds may include trust and safety investigations, counter-exploitation, threat intelligence, investigations of state-linked actors, or adversarial testing of AI safeguards. You do not need expertise across all of these areas.

 - Have experience investigating adversarial behaviour and translating incomplete, evolving evidence into actionable signals. You can connect individual cases to broader patterns while being explicit about uncertainty and the risk of misidentifying legitimate activity.

 - Are proficient in SQL and Python and have experience writing reliable and efficient production code for detection and data processing. Additional ML or SWE experience is a plus.

 - Can apply quantitative analysis and machine-learning methods to measure risks and evaluate system effectiveness. You understand the limitations of your data and can reason about missed harms, false positives and appropriate interventions. Additional DS/measurement background is a plus.

 - Have experience setting strategy and delivering complex, cross-functional technical projects. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, align people with different priorities and drive work through to completion.

 - Communicate clearly and concisely in writing and conversation. You can explain technical findings, make actionable recommendations and surface uncertainty and trade-offs to different audiences.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

 - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

 - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

 - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

 - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

We’re looking for a Software Security Architect to define the security architecture for OpenAI’s next-generation operating system. You’ll work alongside hardware security architects and partner with operating system, silicon, firmware, privacy, and product teams to protect users, their devices, and their data.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. Your work will shape the platform’s trust model, protect sensitive information, and set the technical foundations for AI that is safe, private, and under user control.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define the operating system’s security architecture, trust boundaries, privilege model, and protections for sensitive user data.

 - Partner with hardware security architects to integrate roots of trust, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and processor security capabilities into the operating system.

 - Deep experience designing or securing operating systems, kernels, embedded platforms, hypervisors, or other privileged systems software.

 - Experience building security architectures that span hardware, firmware, operating systems, applications, and cloud services.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Bring practical expertise in secure boot, code signing, device identity, attestation, trusted execution, and hardware-backed key protection.

 - Can write or review systems code in C, C++, Rust, or comparable languages, with a strong grasp of secure development and exploit mitigation.

 - Build rigorous threat models, influence cross-functional engineering teams, and communicate security tradeoffs clearly.

description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Technical Certification Lead, you will lead the design, development, and ongoing quality of OpenAI’s technical role-based certifications. Your work will make clear what each certification validates and what candidates must demonstrate to earn it.

This is a hands-on people manager role on the Certification team. You will manage the Certification Assessment Specialists building technical assessments across the certification portfolio, setting priorities, coaching team members, and holding the team accountable for quality and delivery. You will personally turn shared certification frameworks into certification-specific competency models, job-task analyses, assessment blueprints, scoring rubrics, and passing criteria.

You will apply program-wide certification standards to individual technical certifications and partner with operations and platform teams to prepare assessments for delivery. You will align learning content to competency models and blueprints while keeping confidential assessment content separate from learning development.

You will take certifications from role analysis through pilot, launch readiness, and ongoing maintenance. As AI tools and technical roles evolve, you will keep the assessments relevant to the work people actually do.

Success means each certification makes a clear claim about what someone can do, the assessment supports that claim, and the curriculum gives candidates a practical way to build the skills they need.

In this role, you will:

 - Build and maintain competency models and facilitate job-task analyses for technical roles. Work with practitioners and subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify critical tasks, define the skills and proficiency each role requires, and keep the models current.

 - Define and maintain assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics. Translate competencies into realistic tasks, define what evidence candidates must produce, and set clear criteria for evaluating performance in line with shared certification standards.

 - Lead standard-setting with subject matter experts and a psychometrician or measurement specialist, using a shared methodology to recommend the passing standard for each assessment.

 - Validate AI-assisted scoring against judgments from calibrated human reviewers. Define when scores require human review, and revalidate scoring after material changes to the model, assessment task, or rubric.

 - Manage and develop Certification Assessment Specialists across technical certifications. Set priorities, review their work, and guide the build and maintenance of assessment tasks, environments, evidence capture, and scoring workflows.

 - Secure and manage SME commitments for role analysis, task design, technical review, pilot feedback, and maintenance. Define what each expert is contributing and when it is needed.

 - Share competency models and permitted blueprint information with learning content developers, and review their content for alignment. Coordinate assessment and curriculum changes through the technical lead rather than direct sharing of confidential assessment details between assessment and learning teams.

 - Own ongoing assessment quality for each technical certification within shared program standards. Use pilot results, scoring consistency, technical reviews, and candidate feedback to identify issues. Partner with certification and measurement teams to calibrate rubrics and decide what needs updating or revalidation.

 - Provide technical input when candidates challenge an assessment task. Partner with operations to oversee fixes and validation for confirmed defects.

 - Define what credential holders must demonstrate to stay certified, when they must demonstrate it, and what evidence counts. Work with the team to align those requirements with shared standards, and with learning, platform, and operations teams to make appropriate renewal options available.

 - Make evidence-based readiness recommendations for pilots, launches, and updates. Document what has been tested, what risks remain, and which issues must be resolved before release. Coordinate technical handoff and delivery readiness with operations and platform teams.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have led the development and maintenance of role-based technical certifications or other high-stakes technical assessments, from role analysis through pilot, launch, and post-launch improvement.

 - Have directly managed and developed engineers or technical assessment specialists, including setting priorities, providing performance feedback, and improving the quality of the team’s work.

 - Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

 - Have personally built competency models, facilitated job-task analyses, and used them to define assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics.

 - Have designed hands-on assessments for software engineering, AI, cloud, or technical implementation roles, and can distinguish authentic evidence of capability from completion of a task.

 - Have built or validated AI-assisted scoring for assessments, with appropriate human review.

 - Have recruited and coordinated subject matter experts across teams, secured their time, and turned differing expert views into clear assessment decisions.

 - Have used evidence from pilots and live assessments to improve tasks and scoring, and can explain what would make you recommend a launch, a narrower pilot, or a delay.

 - Have worked with learning content developers to map curriculum and practice to competencies while maintaining the separation between preparation and assessment content.

 - Communicate technical and measurement tradeoffs clearly to engineers, learning teams, operations partners, and leaders.

 - Can review technical assessment work directly and coach others through design decisions without becoming the bottleneck.

 - Have maintained multiple technical assessments as products, tools, or job expectations changed, and know when to update or retire a task.

 - Care deeply about accessible assessments, consistent scoring, and making only the claims the evidence supports.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

 - Designing practical assessments for AI application development, agentic workflows, or customer-facing AI deployments.

 - Working with psychometricians on standard setting, rubric calibration, or validation of performance assessments.

 - Launching hands-on assessments across live and virtual delivery environments.

title: Treasury, Trade Finance & Cash Flow Forecasting
location: San Francisco; New York City; Seattle
description:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.

The Treasury team is responsible for protecting liquidity, enabling scale, maintaining strong controls, and helping the company operate with clarity and resilience. We work across finance and operational partners to ensure funds move safely, visibility remains high, and Treasury infrastructure keeps pace with a fast-moving business. As hands-on operators and builders, we combine financial judgment with AI, automation, and data to solve problems faster, strengthen controls, and continuously improve how Treasury operates.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior hire to help structure financing for major deals, improve working capital, and lead cash forecasting and liquidity planning. Reporting to the Treasurer, you’ll partner with Compute and teams across OpenAI to design creative financing and payment solutions that support the company’s growth. AI and automation will be core to how you build and scale this capability.

This role can be based in San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Structure and negotiate trade finance solutions that improve deal economics and manage risk.

 - Improve cash conversion by working with Billing, Collections, Accounting, and business teams to bill sooner, collect faster, improve supplier terms, and reduce unnecessary deposits or inventory commitments.

 - Free up cash and credit capacity by managing collateral, letters of credit, guarantees, and renewals.

 - Build direct cash forecasts by incorporating business-specific receipts and payments, compute commitments, and financing timing.

 - Partner with Treasury’s Investment team to determine liquidity buffers, investment decisions, and contingency funding plans.

 - Advise on deal structuring Compute, Finance, and Legal, then coordinate execution with Treasury Operations.

 - Improve e-commerce payment economics with Product, Payments, and Strategic Finance, balancing cost, acceptance, risk, and settlement timing.

 - Recommend billing, collection, prepayment, and credit terms for new business models, balancing cash protection with ease of purchase.

 - Use AI and automation to streamline contract review, credit support tracking, cash forecasting, and treasury workflows.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 10+ years of progressive experience in corporate treasury or banking, including trade finance structuring, working capital management, and cash flow forecasting.

 - A strong track record of negotiating and implementing complex trade finance across multiple instruments.

 - Experience delivering measurable cash conversion improvements through billing, collections, supplier terms, or inventory.

 - Sound judgment on contracts, risk, and approvals, and the ability to explain trade-offs to senior leaders and align business, finance, and legal teams.

 - Built direct cash flow forecasts and reconciled them to an indirect forecast or cash flow statement, with a strong grasp of how commercial terms and balance sheet changes affect liquidity.

 - Leveraged AI or automation to improve finance workflows end-to-end. 

 - Experience in infrastructure, hardware, or other capital-intensive businesses, or familiarity with global e-commerce payments (preferred but not required).

ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

A team that has your back. You’ll work alongside people who help each other out—not just clock in and out.

Every day is a little different, and we’ll train you on all of it:
Receive, unpack, and inspect merchandise using easy-to-learn computer systems
Pick, pack, and ship customer orders
Process returns and keep inventory accurate
Team up with fellow associates and flag issues to your manager

Responsibilities Serve as the primary point of contact for owners, managing the service experience from initial appointment scheduling to vehicle handover. Listen actively to understand owner concerns, accurately document them in the repair order, and set clear expectations for the visit. Translate technical information from technicians into simple, understandable language for owners. Proactively communicate updates on vehicle status, managing timelines and ensuring a transparent process. Coordinate with the Parts and Production teams to ensure all aspects of the service visit are aligned. Prepare and explain estimates and invoices with clarity and accuracy. Assist in warranty repairs and ensure compliance with state and federal automotive repair laws. Manage relationships with third-party vendors, documenting work orders and coordinating with production team to ensure seamless after-hours service completion. Proficient with laptops, computers, and modern software suites (Windows, Google Workspace, Mac, CRM systems, etc.). Exceptional organizational skills, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passion for creating order. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary General Summary This position is tailored for an experienced, high-level Senior Field Service Technician who will serve as a technical expert and leader in supporting complex vehicle repairs and field operations. The role requires an adaptable, team-oriented leader capable of driving continuous improvement, mentoring junior team members, and tackling complex diagnostic challenges in a fast-paced environment. While based primarily at a service center, this role may involve operating remotely, traveling to remote locations, or working at production plants to provide advanced field support as business needs demand. Candidates will be evaluated against a comprehensive spectrum of advanced technical skills and leadership capabilities. Responsibilities Core Responsibilities Advanced Diagnostics & Complex Repairs: Perform bumper-to-bumper diagnostics, complex repairs, installations, and inspections on vehicles both inside service centers and in field settings (customer sites, mobile routes, or remote locations). Technical Support & Remote Troubleshooting: Provide high-level diagnostic guidance to field service teams and perform remote diagnostics or repairs for issues that can be safely addressed without local vehicle access by evaluating logged vehicle data and technical schematics. Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and train junior technicians and internal partners; foster cross-functional collaboration and lead shop-floor technical problem-solving. Advanced Tools & Methodologies: Utilize specialized diagnostic tools (e.g., PICO-Scope, PCAN, Kavaser Memorator, breakout boxes) to resolve complex electrical, high-voltage, and network faults. Quality & Process Standardization: Conduct thorough road tests to verify repair quality, champion continuous improvement processes, and drive high standards across repair workflows. Parts Operations & Systems: Oversee complex parts operations—including ordering, receiving, inventory management, and billing—to ensure quality and operational efficiency. Documentation & Technical Feedback: Produce high-quality documentation in service support and engineering systems; provide root-cause analysis and actionable feedback to field service engineers and leadership. Customer & Cross-Functional Engagement: Interact professionally with customers, suppliers, and internal teams during escalation resolutions or mobile outreach events. Qualifications Key Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school or vocational program preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including weekends, holidays, early morning, evening, or overnight shifts as required. Ability to travel to regional locations or production plants as needed. Proficient in Windows/Mac environments, work order management systems, and specialized engineering/diagnostic documentation systems. Physical capability to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 lbs). State mechanic certifications where required by jurisdiction (e.g., Michigan certifications in front end, suspension, steering, brakes, electrical, and HVAC). Experience & Leadership: 5 to 8+ years of automotive repair experience preferred, with extensive experience in bumper-to-bumper diagnostics. 3 to 8+ years of hands-on experience working on vehicle High Voltage (HV) systems and HV diagnostic work. Experience in leadership or supervisory roles (e.g., Shop Foreman, Team Lead, or Technical Mentor) preferred. Demonstrated background in continuous improvement, process standardization, and escalation management. Spectrum of Advanced Technical Skills High Voltage (HV) & Power Electronics: Deep understanding of high-voltage architecture, High-Voltage Interlock Loops (HVIL), charging isolation, and safety power-down protocols using appropriate PPE. Capable of diagnosing complex HV faults and isolation issues. Low Voltage & Network Electronics: Advanced knowledge of automotive electronics, CAN and LIN bus network communication, reading/leveraging electrical schematics, and performing precise wiring harness repairs. Chassis, Drivability & Dynamic Systems: Mastery in chassis service (alignments, braking systems) and advanced diagnosis of vehicle dynamics (ABS, traction control, power steering, and Noise, Vibration, and Harshness / NVH concerns). Thermal & HVAC Systems: Comprehensive knowledge of HVAC systems, coolant drain/fill operations, A/C machine usage, 609 refrigerant certification, and diagnosing complex thermal management issues. ADAS & Body/Glass Integration: Proficiency in calibrating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and replacing/adjusting sensors, body panels, and glass to precise manufacturer tolerances. Role Summary The Senior Manager is a critical strategic leader responsible for directing both multi-shift, plant-wide material handling operations and the engineering configuration teams. This role ensures seamless logistical support essential for production, while concurrently leading the team that manages all engineering changes and implements the Plan for Every Part (PFEP) from the Supply Chain Engineering team. Reporting directly to the Director of Material Handling, this individual will build, mentor, and lead a diverse, cross-functional team of subordinate managers, engineers, group leaders, and hourly technicians to drive continuous improvement, operational excellence, and lean material flow. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership & Team Building: Directs, mentors, and builds a comprehensive team consisting of Material Handling Managers, Group Leaders, process engineers, and hourly technicians. Manages all direct reports, designs organizational structures, defines job duties, and provides continuous mentoring, quarterly feedback, and annual performance reviews. Ensures leadership compliance and excellence in safety documentation, ergonomics, employee engagement, training, attendance, overtime management, and performance evaluations. Develops succession planning, cross-functional training, and leadership development programs across operations and engineering functions. Engineering, PFEP & Configuration: Directs the engineering team in the successful implementation and optimization of the Plan for Every Part (PFEP). Holds overall responsibility for the continuous maintenance of all Material Flow systems configuration, including part location and control cycle data in SAP. Monitors and modifies Min-Max levels for replenishment, continuously optimizing for lean flow and accurate inventory controls. Maintains all part and location signage in both the plant and all internally operated warehouse locations. Develops, implements, and maintains department-wide 5T, 5S, and all visual management standards. Receives engineering and overall product change information from NPI and Launch teams, develops comprehensive implementation plans, and coordinates with Production and Material Handling teams to ensure zero disruption to the production schedule. Serves as the primary lead for any concern items raised for the department. Leads the material handling strategy and acts as a project manager for pilot product programs, new model launches, complex model mix activities, and planned shutdown events. Visits customer locations and partner plants during major milestone events to support the teams and strategic initiatives as required. Operations & Continuous Improvement: Evaluates bottlenecks in upstream processes, develops countermeasures for downstream delivery issues, and drives cost reductions through continuous improvement projects. Analyzes department-wide quality and performance metrics, providing analytics to support the smooth execution of material flow processes. Champions and strategically implements the RMS Quality Network across the organization with an emphasis on the five core principles. Oversees the development, updating, and enforcement of department work instructions and standardized work processes. Responsible for the repairs, maintenance, and procurement of material flow equipment (including carts, dollies, and racks) and manages departmental operating budgets. Ensures strict organizational adherence to local, state, and federal laws, as well as corporate goals, objectives, and policies. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, or a related area of study; Master’s degree (MBA or MS) highly preferred. Experience: 7–10 years of progressive leadership experience in material handling, automotive manufacturing, or supply chain logistics, with a proven track record of leading complex teams (including engineers and supervisors). Extensive experience building Material Flow Processes in the automotive manufacturing industry or similar environments. Highly proficient with systems used for designing and executing material flow processes, specifically SAP, PFEPs, AutoCAD, and FlexSim. Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) is preferred. High-level proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook). Strong team orientation, cross-functional collaborative attitude, and ability to set clear tasks and responsibilities. Advanced creative problem-solving skills with the ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Proven track record of meeting strict deadlines, managing departmental budgets, and working effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment. Ability to read, interpret, and write routine reports, documents, governmental regulations, and procedure manuals. Strong presentation skills with the ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or employees. Ability to apply concepts of basic algebra and geometry. Physical Demands & Work Environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, sit, use hands to finger/handle/feel, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear. Occasionally required to walk, climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required include close vision and the ability to adjust focus. Requires travel, driving a motor vehicle, and communicating using telephone and e-mail. Ability to withstand exposure to solvents, fumes, heat, and odors normally associated with paint application. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. This role is for a technical leader with deep expertise in electromagnetic design who can translate demanding radar performance requirements into robust, manufacturable antenna solutions. You will own antenna design from concept through vehicle integration, working across radar architecture, RF hardware, mechanical engineering, signal processing, manufacturing, validation, and suppliers. Expert-level experience with 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulation and optimization tools, such as Ansys HFSS, CST Studio Suite, or equivalent. Role Summary The Collision Repair Service Engineer is responsible for defining collision repairability and service strategies for all body sheet metal components from the earliest stages of new vehicle development through launch and 3rd level field support. This role represents the voice of the collision repair technician, customer, insurer, and certified repair facility in vehicle design decisions, helping Rivian deliver vehicles that are safe, insurable, repairable, and economically viable to restore after a collision. The engineer will leverage RCAR principles, collision repair industry practices, organizational feedback, and service engineering expertise to influence design concepts before key architecture and component decisions are finalized. The role will simplify repair strategies for complex vehicle structures, establish repair-versus-replace recommendations, create service part numbers and if necessary drawings for service unique subassemblies, and own the service bill of materials to enable sourcing for our NPI stakeholders. This position partners closely with Vehicle Engineering, Design, Service NPI, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing, Supply Chain, Technical Publications, Collision R&D, Service Operations, Insurance, and certified collision repair facilities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment. Responsibilities Lead collision repairability assessments for exterior systems and components beginning in concept, architecture, and advanced development phases and continuing through production launch. Evaluate repairability and replacement strategies for body sheet metal, including closures, fenders, quarter panels, body sides, bumper reinforcements, underbody exterior panels, and related structural or cosmetic assemblies. Translate collision repair requirements into clear design inputs, serviceability targets, and trade-off recommendations for Engineering and Design teams. Establish repair-versus-replace strategies that consider technician safety, repair quality, vehicle performance, customer experience, cycle time, parts availability and total repair cost. Apply RCAR standards and principles, along with recognized collision repair practices, to drive service-focused design concepts and improve vehicle insurability. Represent the voice of the technician and customer in design reviews, architecture decisions, development milestone reviews, prototype evaluations, and production readiness activities. Identify complex vehicle structure systems that may create repair challenges and develop simplified, repeatable, and clearly documented repair paths. Define permissible repair methods, limitations, sectioning or replacement boundaries, attachment strategies, joining requirements, corrosion protection, sealing, refinishing, and post-repair verification needs. Assess the impact of mixed materials, adhesives, rivets, welds, fasteners, composites, castings, high-strength steels, aluminum, and other joining or material technologies on collision repair. With the support of engineering define required tools, fixtures, equipment, and consumables for certified collision repair facilities. Participate in hands-on and virtual prototype, pilot, and validation repairs to confirm that proposed repair strategies can be executed safely, consistently, and efficiently in the field. Create and maintain service part numbers for collision-related components, subassemblies, kits, hardware, consumables, and repair-specific parts in the appropriate product lifecycle and service systems. Own the collision repair service bill of materials for new product introduction, ensuring accurate structure, applicability, service intent, supersession logic, interchangeability, and release status. Ensure service BOMs remain aligned with the latest production design, engineering changes, supplier changes, and approved repair strategies through disciplined change management. Define service assembly content and replacement packages where a repair is not technically, economically, or operationally appropriate at the individual component level. Partner with Technical Publications to convert engineering decisions into collision repair procedures, illustrations, labor-impact inputs, parts recommendations, training content, and technical communications. Develop repairability and insurability metrics, track progress through development, and escalate risks that could affect repair cost, repair cycle time, parts availability, facility capability, or customer satisfaction. Lead issue resolution for collision repair concerns using structured problem solving, root-cause analysis, and closed-loop corrective actions. Gather and analyze feedback from technicians, certified repair facilities, insurers, estimators, adjusters, and customers to identify opportunities for design, service content, parts, or process improvement. Coordinate field returns, repair observations, and part analysis to validate assumptions and improve future product designs. Support launch readiness, service introduction, repair network readiness, and field actions related to collision repairability and service parts. Build and maintain standards, playbooks, checklists, and design review tools that institutionalize prediction, prevention, and protection across vehicle programs. Drive change management activities by evaluating service impact, repair strategy, part interchangeability, documentation updates, and disposition of affected service content. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Automotive Technology, a related engineering/technical degree, or equivalent hands-on industry experience. Technical collision repair training, I-CAR training, OEM certification, ASE certification, or equivalent industry credentials are valued. Training or demonstrated proficiency in CAD, PLM, BOM management, technical documentation, or engineering change control is preferred. 8+ years of experience in collision repair, automotive service engineering, body repair, vehicle body structures, repair facility operations, estimating, insurance claims, or a closely related field. Demonstrated hands-on knowledge of collision repair processes for exterior body and trim components. Strong understanding of repair-versus-replace decision-making and the factors that influence vehicle insurability, repair cost, cycle time, safety, and customer experience. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, CAD data, service procedures, parts catalogs, or repair manuals. Experience working with part numbering, bills of material, engineering change management, or product lifecycle management systems. Ability to evaluate repair concepts for feasibility in a certified collision repair facility, including technician access, sequence of operations, tooling, equipment, and facility constraints. Knowledge of automotive materials and joining methods, including steel, aluminum, plastics, composites, adhesives, rivets, welds, and mechanical fasteners. Ability to identify risks in complex vehicle structures and communicate clear, actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to influence design decisions across a cross-functional organization. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple programs, deliverables, and priorities across development phases and locations. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, especially when requirements are incomplete, ambiguous, or technically complex. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Collision repair technician, structural repair, or OEM service engineering experience. Experience applying RCAR standards, procedures, research, or repairability principles. Experience with vehicle exterior systems, body structures, closures, plastics, lighting, glazing, or trim. Experience developing repair procedures, collision repair manuals, service bulletins, and training materials. Experience with PLM, ERP, service parts, BOM management, or engineering release systems. Experience with CATIA or comparable CAD tools; ability to review and communicate from 3D data. Experience with EV architecture, high-voltage vehicle safety, ADAS-related repair considerations, calibration requirements, and post-repair validation. Experience working directly with insurers, estimating platforms, collision repair networks, suppliers, or automotive certification organizations. Join Our Team as an Lean Engineer III!
The Lean Engineer III leads continuous improvement initiatives within assigned value streams to improve process capability, productivity, quality, flow, and operational performance. While applying Lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodologies, and data-driven problem solving, this role analyzes and improves production systems, eliminates waste and variability, and implements sustainable process improvements that support business and manufacturing objectives.
The Lean Engineer III works cross-functionally with operations and functional teams, leads high-impact improvement projects, establishes effective production and problem-solving standards, and builds team capability through coaching and application of continuous improvement practices. This role uses strong analytical, technical, and influencing skills to identify improvement opportunities, facilitate problem solving, and sustain measurable results across manufacturing operations.
Key Responsibilities:
Lean & Six Sigma Improvement Execution: Lead and execute Lean and Six Sigma initiatives within assigned value streams, applying continuous improvement methodologies to improve productivity, quality, process capability, flow, and waste reduction in alignment with operational and business objectives.
Project Leadership & Delivery: Lead cross-functional improvement projects of moderate to high complexity, establishing objectives, coordinating activities, managing implementation, and ensuring measurable improvements are integrated into standard work and sustained over time.
Process Improvement & Problem Solving: Evaluate manufacturing and support processes to identify waste, variation, bottlenecks, and performance gaps; apply structured problem-solving methodologies to determine root causes and implement improvements in quality, cost, flow, and process capability.
Lean & Six Sigma Methodology Application: Apply appropriate Lean and Six Sigma methods, including DMAIC, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Kaizen, 5S, Kanban, Standard Work, visual management, and Root Cause Analysis to improve process performance and operational effectiveness.
Data Analysis & Performance Management: Analyze process and performance data using statistical methods to identify trends, prioritize improvement opportunities, validate results, and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs); communicate actionable findings and recommendations to operational and functional leaders.
Change Management & Sustainment: Partner with leaders and operational teams to implement process changes, build stakeholder ownership, and integrate improvements into standard operating procedures, work instructions, visual management, and other operating systems to support adoption and sustainment.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence:  Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to align improvement priorities, resolve barriers, coordinate implementation, and deliver sustainable results through effective influence without direct authority.
Continuous Improvement Capability Building: Coach project teams and operational stakeholders in structured problem solving and the effective application of Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to strengthen continuous improvement capabilities and reinforce process discipline.
Standardization & Governance: Support consistent application of Lean and Six Sigma methods, standards, and governance within assigned areas, ensuring improvement activities align with enterprise continuous improvement frameworks and local operating requirements.
How You Will Do It:
Identify gaps in business metrics and then work with all levels of the factory value stream in establishing and executing a strategy for improving them
Assess using Value Stream Mapping and root cause problem solving tools (such as A3, 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagram, etc) the current state of the value stream Operations, develop Future State vision and drive and monitor the implementation plan
Develops Lean capability across the value stream by coaching value stream staff, front‑line leaders, and associates in lean principles, strengthening problem‑solving behaviors, operational discipline, and a culture of continuous improvement.
Ensure the implementation and sustainment of the Daily Management system at his/her respective value stream.
Perform time studies of the operations with the goal of re-balancing the operation and eliminating waste.
Modify/update physical and digital layouts as required during the transformation of the site.
Ensure process owner involvement in Standardized Work development and team leadership
Use kaizen funnel tracking and reporting systems to build detailed project plans, drive performance, and ensure transformational and continuous improvement projects finish on time and deliver their goals.
Collaborate with leadership to develop a Lean value stream Transformation Roadmap, driving breakthrough or Best-in-class performance that balances resources between internal plant efficiency and external customer-focused effectiveness projects through “Just Do It” improvements, Kaizens, and Workshops.
Partners with values stream Management team to identify systemic barriers to project success and strategically drive the organizational, process, and behavioral changes required to remove them.
Document improvement process learning and shares best practices throughout the company
Identifies and brings forward to value stream team new project opportunities
Partners with the values stream Manager on strategic initiatives that strengthen standards compliance, accelerate the deployment of new systems, and shape innovative, future‑focused solutions that drive sustainable operational excellence across the value stream.
Additional Functions:
Maintain regular and punctual attendance
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others
Other responsibilities as assigned
Education & Minimum Qualifications
5-7+ years of manufacturing experience, including a minimum of 3 years in Lean Manufacturing roles within fabrication and/or assembly environments.
Continuous Improvement Delivery: Demonstrated success leading and completing cross-functional process improvement projects that deliver measurable gains in safety, quality, cost, delivery, and productivity.
Process Assessment & Planning: Proven ability to assess end-to-end processes; develop project charters and improvement plans; align initiatives with business objectives; and ensure effective use of resources and budget.
Leadership & Influence: Ability to lead, facilitate, coach, and motivate small project teams, guiding stakeholders through change while driving accountability and results.
Data & Statistical Analysis: Strong proficiency in statistical analysis and data interpretation, with the ability to identify trends, validate improvements, and support data-driven decision-making.
Business Acumen: Solid understanding of manufacturing and supply chain economics, with an analytical and pragmatic approach to problem solving that balances impact, cost, and complexity.
Communication: Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to clearly influence and align stakeholders from shop-floor teams to Business Unit leadership.
Practical Problem Solving using A3 or similar methodologies:
Demonstrated judgment in selecting and applying appropriate Lean and problem-solving tools, favoring effective and scalable solutions over unnecessary complexity.
Demonstrated expertise in Lean tools and concepts: VSM, Kaizen facilitation, SMED, 5S, standard work, takt time, flow, pull systems.
Collaboration & Relationship Building: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build trust, navigate conflict, and foster productive partnerships across functions and leadership levels.
Project & Time Management: Proven organizational and project management skills, capable of managing multiple improvement initiatives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Technical Tools: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and statistical tools such as Minitab.
Preferred
Demonstrated experience developing area improvement strategies to meet business KPI targets (Safety, Quality, Delivery & Cost).

description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
As an Adoption Specialist on our Mid-Market team, you are the technical expert our customers and our Account Managers call when a high-value feature needs to go from "purchased" to "running in the operation." You work on a project-scoped basis: each engagement has a defined goal, a timeline, and clear commitments from both Samsara and the customer. Think of the structure of a solutions architect team, delivered as part of the Samsara relationship rather than as a paid service.
You pair deep product and technical knowledge with project management discipline. You dig into a customer's use case, understand how their industry and operating procedures shape the way they use Samsara, and design a practical path to adoption. You translate highly technical concepts into plain language for non-technical audiences, and you hold customers accountable to the milestones that make a project succeed.
You are also a force multiplier for the broader Customer Success organization. Through research, documentation, and coaching, you help Account Managers learn new products and level up their product knowledge, and you work cross-functionally with Support, Product, and Engineering to solve problems and bring customer insight back to the teams building Samsara. Account Managers continue to own the customer relationship and the renewal; you own the project and the adoption outcome.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world : Your efforts will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work : One day you'll be learning how a waste management company dispatches its routes and the next you may be digging into the inner workings of a food distribution center. You want to understand customer operating procedures well enough to shape our products around them.
You thrive the most when solving technical problems : You enjoy diagnosing why something isn't working, researching workarounds, and building a solution that fits a customer's real-world workflow.
You deliver to a deadline : You run projects with clear plans, owners, and dates, and you are comfortable having direct conversations when a customer or internal partner falls behind.
You are a natural teacher : You can take a complex product concept and make it clear for a fleet manager, a safety lead, or an executive, and you enjoy helping teammates build their own expertise.
You are the architect of your own career : This is a new role on a team that is still shaping its future. You will have plenty of autonomy and opportunity to define how the role works and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
You want to be with the best : At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Be a deep Subject Matter Expert on the Samsara product, API, integrations and AI capabilities.
Lead project-scoped adoption engagements with Mid-Market customers, from scoping and kickoff through delivery, to increase adoption of Samsara's technical features and drive measurable customer outcomes.

title: Manufacturing Quality Inspector
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and you're the one who makes sure of it. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in our QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss and confirming that the parts going into our robots match the drawings they came from. Get it right, and every arm we ship starts on solid ground.


What you'll do

- Inspect mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab using GD&T (ASME Y14.5), catching deviations before they turn into downstream problems.

- Program and run CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec.

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change.

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations so quality holds steady as we scale.

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals.

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work.

- Take a seat on the Material Review Board and help resolve mechanical nonconformances.

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, and flag GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework.

- Support our 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab clean, organized, and safe.


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment.

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5.

- Hands-on skill with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates.

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills.

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurements without cutting corners.


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software.

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: cybersecurity analyst senior - vulnerability management
location: 2401 Utah Ave S #800, Seattle, Washington, United States
description:
Now Brewing – cybersecurity analyst senior - vulnerability management! #tobeapartner
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company. One that not only celebrated coffee and the rich tradition, but that also brought a feeling of connection. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who share this passion and are guided by their service to others.
This role contributes to Starbucks success by delivering and supporting Vulnerability Management technology solutions. This role will be responsible for the design and deployment of technology and process solutions, establishing key business capabilities enabling the realization of strategic initiatives and operational improvements.
A successful Senior Vulnerability Management Analyst is a communicator and an investigator. This role will communicate all manner of system and application vulnerabilities to inform patching/fix decisions and velocity for engineers and executives. You will understand perspective on questions and contextualize answers through the lens of cybersecurity, referencing SMEs as needed. You will intuitively know the available dataset and can efficiently dig through data to articulate priority, and shepherd technology owners to success.
As one of the key faces for Vulnerability Management, you will have incredible insight to design a revolutionary approach leveraging the latest technology to quickly analyze and contextualize data at scale. In this role, you will surface trends in data and provide analysis to relevant stakeholders to identify and solve Starbucks most pressing vulnerability management issues.
You will advance threat-informed vulnerability management by leveraging a mix of internal and external vulnerability and criticality sources, including CVE and CVSS. Framed by a detail-oriented approach to reporting, you will apply data science practices to broad swaths of data from roasting to retail, globally.
Highly motivated individuals outside of cybersecurity, but with strong analytical and reporting backgrounds are encouraged to apply.
As a cybersecurity analyst senior - vulnerability management, you will…
Track communication and status with multiple stakeholders across all mediums including email, instant messaging, and meetings. Responding quickly and thoroughly to issues and requests with correct technical information.
Create and update reports and ad hoc queries for identified target audiences, ensuring the right information is available to the right person to effectively inform decision making and remediation.
Stay informed on the latest developments in cybersecurity and know when to escalate vulnerabilities as a global priority. Acting with urgency while modeling and acting in accordance with Starbucks guiding principles and values.
Drive requirements for growing and changing data management and reporting platforms.
Perform application configuration and maintenance (i.e. create attributes, workflows, and UI changes) in support of solution delivery initiatives.
Gather, analyze, and document solution requirements. Facilitate user story creation and backlog grooming in an agile delivery environment.
Be self-directed; are successful with minimal direction from more senior analysts providing escalation when necessary.
Create and maintain systems documentation (e.g. Wiki, Knowledge Base Articles). Develop and facilitate system training for internal and external audiences.
Provide constructive input and perspective to team conversations.

About Stripe

About the team
The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
What you'll do
As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
Responsibilities
Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
Who you are
We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.

5+ years of professional experience in a role requiring diagnostic thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration
Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Proficiency with AI development tools and platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, API integrations, workflow automation tools)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work
Preferred qualifications
Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
Experience in marketing, marketing operations, growth, or a closely adjacent function, including familiarity with marketing technology stacks (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce, analytics platforms, content management tools)

title: Senior Facilities Engineer - Straddle Projects
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:

Engineering Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
Lead the engineering development and execution readiness of Eagle Ford Straddle projects. Owns projects from Project Development handoff through engineering completion and handoff to the Program Manager for execution. Ensure projects have a complete engineering design, construction work package, MOC documentation, and Operations alignment before construction begins.
Key Accountabilities
Engineering owner for all Eagle Ford Straddle projects. Responsible for developing executable project scopes, managing third-party engineering contractors, coordinating Operations and Maintenance input, and delivering construction-ready work packages that support safe, cost-effective project execution.
Program Ownership & Optimization
Own Straddle projects from Project Development handoff through Program Manager handoff.
Develop project scope, engineering basis, design packages, and construction-ready deliverables.
Apply consistent engineering standards, lessons learned, and best practices across Straddle program.
Identify and mitigate engineering, constructability, operational, and execution risks early in project
Vendor Relationships & Performance Management
Lead the third-party engineering contractor through the engineering phase of each Straddle project.
Define engineering deliverables, expectations, review cycles, and quality requirements.
Coordinate development of engineering drawings, construction work packs, material takeoffs, tie-in packages, P&IDs, plot plans, electrical and instrumentation details, and other project-specific deliverables as required.
Review contractor deliverables for technical quality, completeness, constructability, and alignment with BPX expectations.
Drive timely resolution of engineering questions, design issues, scope gaps, and field conflicts.
Hold the engineering contractor accountable for quality, responsiveness, and schedule performance.
Engineering and Construction Work Pack Development
Develop complete engineering and construction work packages.
Coordinate constructability reviews with Construction, Operations, and Maintenance teams.
Ensure packages include scope definition, tie-in requirements, isolation plans, material requirements, and execution considerations.
Identify long-lead materials, critical path items, and execution constraints.
Budget Forecasting & Cost Management
Forecast annual program budgets - bottom-up by equipment count, rate, and duration
Track actuals vs. forecast monthly; identify and explain variances
Provide budget inputs to Program Engineering TL for total spend reporting
Identify cost reduction opportunities within each program without compromising performance
Operations and Maintenance Engagement
Engage Operations and Maintenance throughout project development.
Lead field walkthroughs and design reviews.
Incorporate field feedback into project designs and construction packages.
Ensure projects support safe operation, maintainability, and long-term reliability.
Management of Change Ownership
Create and steward Management of Change documentation for each Straddle project.
Ensure MOCs accurately capture the project scope, technical basis, affected equipment, operating impact, safety considerations, documentation updates, and required approvals.
Coordinate with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Construction, HSE, and other stakeholders to complete required MOC reviews.
Track MOC progress and ensure required documentation is complete before project execution.
Confirm that drawings, operating procedures, equipment records, and other controlled documents are updated as required through the MOC process.
Ensure MOC documentation is structured consistently across all Eagle Ford Straddle projects.
Project Development to Execution Handoff
Deliver complete handoff packages to the Program Manager for execution.
Clearly communicate project scope, risks, assumptions, material requirements, and key decisions.
Support project execution by resolving engineering questions and design clarifications.
Capture lessons learned and incorporate improvements into future projects.
Scope, Cost, and Schedule Support
Support project estimating, AFE development, and execution planning.
Identify cost, schedule, and constructability risks.
Drive standardization opportunities that improve execution efficiency and reduce cost.
Essential Experience and Education
Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering
7+ years of engineering experience supporting upstream oil and gas production facilities, midstream facilities, or comparable process facilities.
Demonstrated experience serving as a Project Engineer or Facilities Engineer responsible for developing projects from early scope definition through construction-ready design.
Strong brownfield facility modification experience, including tie-ins, equipment additions, piping modifications, instrumentation, electrical/controls interfaces, and integration with operating facilities.
Experience developing and reviewing P&IDs, plot plans, equipment specifications, piping plans, tie-in packages, material takeoffs, construction work packs, and other engineering deliverables.
Experience leading HAZOP/PHA, constructability, design, MOC, PSSR, and project-readiness reviews for operating facilities.
Experience leading and managing third-party engineering contractors, including defining scope, reviewing deliverables, managing technical comments, resolving design issues, and maintaining engineering schedules.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate engineering across multiple disciplines, including mechanical, piping, civil/structural, electrical, instrumentation, controls, and automation.
Experience working directly with Operations, Maintenance, Construction, HSE, Automation, and other engineering disciplines during project development.
Hands-on experience with Management of Change (MOC) processes for modifications to operating facilities.
Experience conducting field walkthroughs, constructability reviews, design reviews, and project readiness reviews.
Experience identifying long-lead materials, tie-in constraints, operational impacts, constructability issues, and execution risks before construction.
Working experience with project estimating, AFE development, forecasting, cost tracking, procurement support, and schedule development.
Experience supporting projects by resolving RFIs, field conflicts, design clarifications, and scope changes.
Desirable Criteria
Direct experience developing and executing brownfield compression projects, including compressor installations, inlet separation, suction and discharge piping, coolers, control valves, measurement, instrumentation, electrical systems, and facility controls.
Experience taking projects through the full engineering lifecycle, from initial field walk and scope development through detailed engineering, MOC, procurement, construction-ready work packs, execution support, commissioning, and startup.
Demonstrated experience acting as the owner's engineer while managing third-party EPC or engineering contractors, including establishing deliverables, reviewing engineering quality, challenging designs, controlling scope, and driving schedule performance.
